jobs.excerpt: The Senior Asset Manager, Commercial Servicing will provide proactive monitoring and surveillance of assigned assets securing Commercial Real Estate (“CRE”) loans, as well as being a source of information and training for Asset Managers.
jobs.description:
The Senior Asset Manager, Commercial Servicing will provide proactive monitoring and surveillance of assigned assets securing Commercial Real Estate (“CRE”) loans, as well as being a source of information and training for Asset Managers. This is an individual contributor role that reports to a manager and will work hand-in-hand with various internal business units. The Senior Asset Manager will serve as the point of contact for the borrower and the assigned investor(s), provide oversight of an assigned portfolio, facilitate borrower requests, monitor and enforce loan covenants, resolve insurance non-compliance, complete financial analyses, delinquency resolution, be an escalation point for questions and inquiries from external clients and internal staff, and other responsibilities as need arises. This position requires the ability to provide best-in-industry customer service, interpret loan documents, compliance, quality control, provide mentorship to team members, and resolve a wide spectrum of borrower-related inquiries related to commercial loan servicing. This is a customer-facing position, and all interactions must be handled with a high degree of professionalism, courteous customer service, and promptness. Individuals in this role are required to adhere to investor servicing guidelines, internal policies and procedures.

Job Responsibilities and Requirements:

Customer Service:

  • Act as the primary contact for the borrower, investor, related third parties, and various internal business units in order to resolve all inquiries and servicing functions for the loan.
  • Maintain professionalism during all interactions.
  • Demonstrated ability to initiate difficult conversations while maintaining best-in-class customer service.
  • Demonstrated ability to handle escalated items during difficult conversations.

Portfolio and Asset Oversight and Servicing:

  • Quality Control check of loan boarding against the loan documents to ensure accuracy.
  • Coach team members on CRE loan document interpretation.
  • Identify & monitor loan covenants for borrower compliance to include letter of credit monitoring, cash management provisions, waterfall allocation, DSCR testing, occupancy triggers, etc.
  • Monitor Letters of Credit for expiration.
  • Interpret and work effectively with large data sets.
  • Expert monitoring of escrow and reserve functions within the CRE environment.
  • Work within a CRE loan servicing system and maintain data integrity.
  • Read, understand, and proactively monitor rent rolls, financial statements, property inspections, and other documents in order to address potential performance issues before they arise.
  • Strong knowledge of CRE loan participations.
  • Strong knowledge of CRE insurance coverage requirements.
  • Spread and analyze property level financial statements and provide training to Asset Managers for complex assets.
  • Create a pro forma based upon historical property performance and provide training to Asset Managers for complex assets.
  • Work closely with borrowers and investors to resolve delinquent payment issues as they arise.
  • Generate an amortization table and calculate various loan accounting items including, but not limited to, interest, default interest, prepayment premiums, yield maintenance, and escrow constants with no assistance.
  • Create, maintain, and monitor investor level watchlist.
  • Lead client calls and/or meetings reviewing loan performance issues.
  • Review loan draws submitted by the Borrower for accuracy and overall construction / renovation schedules and provide training to Asset Managers for complex draws.
  • Administer construction / rehab loan covenants, including periodic review of construction/rehab work schedule, progress reports and inspections, property stabilization performance schedules, budgets, and borrower equity earnout provisions
  • Proactive engagement with borrower regarding exit strategy and current market conditions as projects progress towards maturity.
  • Escalate items appropriately to Manager.
  • Prepare, Collaborate with Investor Reporting, and Review CREF-C Reporting Packages
  • Act as the first point of contact for all escalations from the team.

Complete Borrowers Requests:

  • Read and interpret CRE loan documents to determine Borrower Request eligibility.
  • Discuss and engage in conversations with borrowers and investors regarding borrower request submissions, requirements, and resolution with no assistance.
  • Exceptional understanding of additional document requirements for various borrower requests, including the ability to teach and mentor team members in their understanding.
  • Complete presentation-level write-ups and recommendations for various types of borrower requests.
  • Review and Approve write-ups completed by Asset Managers prior to presentation.
  • Exceptional familiarity with the following requests, documentation requirements, and processes:
  • Assumption
  • Collateral Substitution
  • Insurance Loss Processing
  • Insurance Non-Compliance Resolution and Waivers
  • Lender Placed Insurance
  • Loan Maturity Extension
  • Loan Modification
  • Partial Release of Collateral
  • Property Management Change

Other Responsibilities and Requirements:

  • Adapt quickly to various requests from multiple sources.
  • Prioritize multiple, simultaneous incoming requests.
  • Generate reports for investors as required.
  • Coordinate with internal departments for servicing functions as required.
  • Review and update internal policies and procedures as required.
  • Assist with audits as requested.
  • Lead team trainings.
  • Prepare presentation for investors, management, and internal business units.
  • Other duties as assigned.
  • Qualifications
  • Demonstrates positive attitude, adds to a positive team morale, and is eager to take on and learn new things

  • Minimum of 8 years of CRE loan servicing experience required, 1 – 2 years in a leadership position preferred.

  • Strong proficiency in Word, Excel, Outlook, CoPilot, and other information processing programs

The LPN Care Team Member is responsible for conducting Chronic Care Management (CCM) outreach to patients with two or more chronic conditions. This role supports ongoing care coordination, improves patient outcomes, reduces avoidable hospitalizations and emergency department utilization, and promotes patient engagement through structured monthly outreach, education, care plan management and promotes patient well-being through timely follow-up, education, and coordination of services.

Entity

MUSC Community Physicians (MCP)

Employee

Hourly

Job Description


Chronic Care Management (CCM)


Key Responsibilities

• Conduct monthly telephonic outreach to assigned CCM patient panel
• Complete a minimum of 20 minutes of non–face-to-face care management services per patient per calendar month
• Perform at least two outreach attempts for patients not reached
• Assess patient status, including changes in condition, symptoms, or care needs
• Review and reinforce individualized care plans and patient goals
• Support medication adherence and identify potential medication concerns
• Identify and address barriers to care (e.g., transportation, access to medications, social needs)

• Escalate clinical concerns to appropriate clinical support staff or providers per workflow standards
• Document all interactions accurately in the electronic health record (EHR) and track time for billing compliance

Care Coordination & Patient Engagement

• Provide education on chronic disease management and preventive care
• Encourage patient participation in primary care and adherence to treatment plans
• Monitor for signs of deterioration and escalate concerns appropriately
• Support transitions of care when applicable
• Promote patient self-management and engagement in their health

Required Skills & Competencies

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills
• Ability to assess patient needs and apply clinical judgment appropriately
• Proficiency in EHR documentation and care coordination workflows (experience with Epic Systems preferred)
• Knowledge of chronic disease management and population health principles
• Ability to manage a high-volume patient panel efficiently
• Strong organizational and time management skills
• Ability to work independently within established workflows and SOPs
• Ability to appropriately route communication to providers vs. clinical support teams

Qualifications

• Active LPN licensure in good standing (South Carolina preferred)
• BLS (Basic Life Support) certification (if required by role)
• Prior experience in care coordination, case management, ambulatory care, or chronic disease management preferred
• Experience working with high-risk or chronic condition populations strongly preferred

jobs.description:
Job Summary

At Fuze Health, we put patients first and tirelessly address the most pressing needs in healthcare. We empower millions to digitally connect with care providers, essential health resources and needed treatments – and enable care providers, employers, health plans and life sciences companies to meaningfully enhance quality, outcomes and value. We are dedicated to helping our partners evolve and modernize to meet emerging patient and marketplace needs.

Fuze Health’s foundation is built upon the strategic combination of several proven, technology-powered innovators in the digital health, diagnostics, and pharmacy sectors. Our growing portfolio brings together the capabilities of industry leaders including LetsGetChecked, Truepill, and Alto Pharmacy, to create a distinctive, unified force in healthcare. Together, we have the shared vision, advanced capabilities and talented teams to deliver next-generation solutions that patients and healthcare partners need today and into the future.



Job Description

The Product Manager at FuzeRx is an individual contributor responsible for defining and delivering product initiatives that advance patient care, pharmacy operations, and strategic growth. This role sits within the Product Management job family and will support our Care and Partnerships teams.

As a Product Manager, you will own the roadmap for your product area, partnering closely with Engineering, Design, Clinical, Pharmacy Operations, Data, and Business stakeholders to solve meaningful problems for patients and partners. You'll operate with increasing autonomy — driving discovery, prioritization, and execution end-to-end within your domain — while collaborating with senior product leaders on strategy and measurable outcomes aligned with FuzeRx's mission.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own delivery of product features end-to-end — from requirements and design through launch and iteration — within a defined product strategy

  • Translate business, clinical, and operational needs into clear, concise product requirements and specs, partnering with Engineering, Design, and Data

  • Drive feature discussions with customers, engineers, and cross-functional partners (e.g., Clinical, Compliance, Finance), seeking direction from senior product leaders when navigating ambiguity

  • Support product discovery through customer research, data analysis, and validation to ensure features solve real user problems

  • Monitor feature-level success metrics (KPIs, adoption, usability) and use insights to iterate; may own OKR/QBR reporting for your area

  • Optimize roadmap intake — triaging features, bugs, and requests — and connect engineering work to the end-user experience

  • Understand the technologies in your product area; articulate technical requirements and flag risks in design choices

  • Build awareness of regulatory and operational constraints in healthcare and pharmacy, escalating compliance considerations early

Required Experience & Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, Health Informatics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • 2+ years of experience in Product Management or a product-adjacent role (e.g., program management, clinical operations, analytics)

  • Experience shipping product features in partnership with Engineering teams in agile environments

  • Strong analytical skills, with experience using product metrics (KPIs, adoption, usability) to inform decisions

  • Clear, concise communication skills — able to write effective specs and drive feature discussions with engineers, customers, and cross-functional partners

  • Proficiency with common product and collaboration tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Figma, Productboard)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3–6 years of product experience, including features delivered end-to-end from requirements through launch and iteration

  • Experience in regulated or complex domains (e.g., healthcare, pharmacy, fintech)

  • Experience building products for pharmacy, healthcare services, or medication management platforms

  • Familiarity with data-driven personalization, automation, or AI-enabled product capabilities

  • Ability to identify technical risks and articulate technical requirements for features and APIs



Additional Information

Physical requirements for this role include the ability to work at a computer terminal with monitor, keyboard and mouse for extended periods of time, stoop, bend, and reach for equipment and supplies, make frequent repetitive motions required to operate a computer that include the wrists, hands and fingers, and lift, carry, push, pull, and move light objects up to 20 pounds. The role also requires the ability to effectively communicate through verbal interactions, discern auditory information, and visually perceive details to perform essential job functions.


Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and similar applicable state laws, it is Fuze Health’s policy to provide reasonable accommodation to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship.


Salary and Benefits


Salary Range: $140,000-$175,000

Commission Eligible: No

Travel: No - Required up to 0% of the time


Location Requirement: Alto is limited to individuals residing in the following states: Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Florida, Kansas, Maryland, Missouri, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Washington (WA), and Wisconsin.


Employment Authorization Requirement: Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.


Benefits: Full-time employee benefits include: dental, vision, and multiple group medical plans to choose from, a 401(k) retirement savings plan, group life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, flexible spending account (FSA) and health savings account (HSA), commuter benefits, employer-paid short-term (STD) and long-term disability (LTD) insurance, and additional supplemental insurance plans (spouse life insurance, legal insurance, an employee assistance program, home health testing kits, and a fertility medication discount program). Employees are also provided flexible vacation time, accrued paid sick time, 10 paid holidays, (2 floating holidays for full time non-exempt employees) , and eight weeks of paid parental leave for eligible employees, additional paid weeks for the birthing parent, 4 weeks paid caregiver leave, and a Lifestyle Spending Account allowance each month.


More Benefits Information Here: Fuze Health Benefits Site.


Application deadline: October 22, 2026



Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.excerpt: Location Remote in Europe, ideally Zurich or London.
jobs.description:
Location
Remote in Europe, ideally Zurich or London. Travels up to 30%. Reports to the CEO.

Albatross

Albatross builds perception models: AI that understands human behavior and powers product discovery the way a great salesperson does, by observing the customer and adapting in real time. LLMs understand words. We understand behavior.

Our models power discovery for 50 million+ shoppers a month. The results are public. Wallapop: +119% homepage engagement, +35% overall engagement. OfferUp: +84% homepage engagement, +20% overall engagement.

One platform, four primitives: discovery feed, similar items, playlist, contextual search. A customer goes live in seven weeks. The pipeline is global, we are deployed in 12 countries.

About the Job

Our results sell Albatross. Your job is to get every customer to them, fast, and turn them into revenue. You own everything after signature: the seven weeks to a live A/B test, the result the customer can measure, the conversion to a long-term contract, the renewal, and the growth after it, use case by use case and marketplace by marketplace.

Velocity is the key: a customer who goes live in seven weeks and sees the lift in week eight renews and expands. Until customers see the results, you and your team are the reason they trust us. Maintain that trust and bring them fast to the results.

The platform is the product: four primitives, one platform, configured, not coded. You make sure customers use what we built, as designed. Every customer that goes live without custom code is a customer we can scale to. Your team is what lets us add customers without adding engineers, and it is never the bottleneck.

We want a builder. Today the founders and the data scientists run deployments. You take that over, build the Deployment Strategist team that runs it, and turn it into a machine: one strategist per five customers, every customer on all four primitives.

You own the customer. Sales hands over at signature and does not take it back. You will:

  • Own every customer relationship after signature, as the senior point of contact for their CPO, VP of Data and VP of Engineering.
  • Run every pilot to a result: live A/B test in seven weeks, uplift measured, contract converted.
  • Keep customers on the platform: primitives and platform components as designed, configuration over custom code. When a customer asks for bespoke work, you find the way to do it with what exists, or you say no.
  • Own renewals and upsells: every live customer to all primitives, and group agreements rolled out to every marketplace the group owns. You handle customer QBRs and show impact.
  • Own customer support: one front door, fast answers, incidents handled with the customer informed before they ask.
  • Hire, build and lead the Deployment Strategist team across Europe and the US. The first is already hired.
  • Turn every customer into a reference: case studies, press releases, a CPO who takes the call from the next prospect.

Requirements

Who you are

  • You come from software. You have deployed a SaaS or API product into enterprise customers, and you know the difference between building bespoke solutions and configuring a platform.
  • You have built a customer success, deployment or solutions function from zero at a startup, and you ran it on numbers: time to live, pilot-to-contract conversion, net revenue retention.
  • You have owned renewals and expansion for enterprise customers, with the numbers to show it.
  • You have hired and led a technical, customer-facing team: solutions engineers, implementation consultants, forward deployed engineers or data analysts.
  • You are technical. You can read an A/B test, you know what data a model needs, and you can guide the analysis yourself. Our customers' VPs of Data will test you.
  • You move fast and you hold the line. You do not overpromise, you do not let scope grow, and you get to a strong result fast and iterate from there.
  • You stay calm when the page is down. If we are down, the customer's homepage is down. We own their critical path.
  • You have worked with marketplaces, e-commerce, or search, personalisation or recommendation products. A strong plus, not a must.
  • You like to travel. Human contact is irreplaceable.
  • You are eligible to work in Europe.

The motion is proven. You make it run without the founders, then you make it faster.

What success looks like

3 months:

  • Every live customer and every active pilot knows you as their point of contact, and you have met them in person.
  • The deployment playbook is written: what a strategist does from kickoff to A/B readout, with no custom code in it.
  • Support has one front door and a response time customers can quote.
  • The second Deployment Strategists is hired.

12 months:

  • Pilots convert into long-term contracts at a rate the business can plan on, and deployments go live in less than five weeks.
  • Every live customer runs all four primitives, or has a dated plan to get there.
  • Every production customer is a reference, and at least three are public case studies.
  • The Deployment Strategist team runs customer deployments on its own, and the customer count has grown without your team.

Benefits

  • Europe-based: total at target €180-230k (€140k-€170k gross base salary + €40k - €60k variable at target).
  • Equity, four-year vesting, one-year cliff.
  • Full remote flexibility across Europe.

Position Summary:

To lead the Internal Audit function by developing and executing a risk-based internal audit plan, evaluating the effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal control systems, ensuring timely closure of audit observations, strengthening policy governance, and providing independent assurance to the Audit Committee and senior management.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement the annual risk-based Internal Audit Plan aligned with organizational objectives and key business risks.
  • Lead financial, operational, compliance, process, and special audits across all business functions.
  • Ensure timely execution of audit assignments and preparation of accurate, objective, and actionable audit reports.

Career Category

Job Description

Live

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. Amgen is seeking a Senior Director, Content and Audience Strategy to define and lead enterprise content and audience strategy across commercial and stakeholder engagement channels. This leader will translate complex business needs and transformation initiatives into scalable, personalized, and governance-compliant content solutions.

The Senior Director will build and lead a high-performing content and audience strategy function, bringing together content strategy, audience analytics, production, taxonomy, metadata, governance, and stakeholder management. The role will partner with business and portfolio leads, digital product managers, and transformation stakeholders to turn business use cases into audience-driven content strategies and coordinated, multi-channel roadmaps.

This leader will establish the standards, operating models, and governance frameworks needed to connect audience needs with content production capabilities, channel requirements, brand messaging, regulatory expectations, and measurable business outcomes. The role will also oversee content production strategy and external partner relationships, while guiding the integration and adoption of taxonomy, metadata, content management, and audience intelligence capabilities across the enterprise.

The Senior Director will represent content and audience strategy in executive forums and transformation governance, creating clear decision materials, surfacing dependencies and risks, and helping teams sustain momentum through complex, multi-year change.

Key Responsibilities

Content and Audience Strategy

  • Lead a high-performing content and audience strategy function with strong capabilities in content strategy, audience analytics, and stakeholder management.
  • Structure, hire, develop, and performance-manage the content and audience strategy team.
  • Partner with business leads, portfolio leads, digital product managers, and transformation stakeholders to translate business use cases into audience-driven content strategies and multi-channel content roadmaps.
  • Develop an integrated content architecture that connects audience needs, production and channel capabilities, brand messaging, regulatory requirements, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Assess content operational maturity, production complexity, technology readiness, governance requirements, and transformation dependencies for content-driven initiatives.
  • Set enterprise standards for audience segmentation, content strategy, and content governance.

Content Production Leadership and Oversight

  • Define production strategies and roadmaps aligned with content priorities and audience engagement plans.
  • Establish reusable content standards, governance frameworks, and quality assurance processes that support brand consistency, regulatory compliance, and efficient medical and legal review.
  • Partner with creative, marketing operations, medical, legal, compliance, privacy, brand, and digital teams to ensure content is brand-aligned, compliant, and production-ready.
  • Oversee channel-specific content production requirements and templates for HCP, patient, customer, and internal stakeholder audiences.
  • Manage relationships with external creative agencies, translation services, production vendors, and platform partners; establish service levels, quality standards, and cost benchmarks.

Taxonomy and Metadata Leadership and Oversight

  • Define the strategic direction for enterprise taxonomy frameworks that classify content, audiences, channels, and business domains in alignment with commercial strategy and transformation initiatives.
  • Provide guidance on metadata standards and governance requirements, and oversee their implementation and maintenance across content systems.
  • Guide the integration of taxonomy and metadata into content management systems, customer data platforms, and marketing automation tools, working with technology partners as needed.
  • Monitor taxonomy and metadata quality through regular reviews and reporting, identify improvement opportunities, and hold the team accountable for continuous improvement.
  • Lead and develop the taxonomy and metadata management team, ensuring it has the skills, tools, authority, and support to maintain enterprise standards and respond to evolving business needs.

Transformation Adoption and Governance

  • Drive enterprise adoption of content platforms, content management systems, taxonomy and metadata standards, and audience intelligence tools by communicating their value and setting clear expectations.
  • Own and maintain the portfolio transformation roadmap, including dependencies, milestones, risks, and budget tracking.
  • Represent content and audience strategy in governance forums with business leads, portfolio leads, digital product managers, and transformation stakeholders; surface decisions, escalate blockers, and document progress.
  • Manage cross-pillar interdependencies and help teams anticipate upcoming needs and risks.
  • Build and execute communication strategies that support enablement across groups, including role clarity, onboarding, and workflow integration.
  • Coordinate with key partners to support delivery accountability and value realization.
  • Track and report on planned milestones, and maintain the future-state strategic vision, milestones, workforce strategy inputs, and investment projections.

Executive Communication

  • Represent content strategy in executive forums, portfolio reviews, and transformation governance discussions.
  • Guide the transformation narrative to sustain organizational momentum and leadership confidence.
  • Create executive-ready decision materials that clearly communicate strategic options and business impact.
  • Lead stakeholder readiness planning across business, technology, and measurement groups to support adoption of new ways of working.

Win

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The leader we seek is an experienced, audience-centric strategist who can connect content, data, technology, and business transformation. They bring the judgment to set enterprise direction, the ability to build and develop strong teams, and the influence to align senior stakeholders across a complex, matrixed organization.

Basic Qualifications

  • Doctorate degree and 5 years of experience in marketing technology, digital transformation, or enterprise program management; OR
  • Master’s degree and 8 years of experience in marketing technology, digital transformation, or enterprise program management; OR
  • Bachelor’s degree and 10 years of experience in marketing technology, digital transformation, or enterprise program management; OR
  • Associate’s degree and 14 years of experience in marketing technology, digital transformation, or enterprise program management; OR
  • High school diploma / GED and 16 years of experience in marketing technology, digital transformation, or enterprise program management.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 12 or more years of progressive experience in marketing technology, digital transformation, or enterprise program management, including at least five years at the Senior Director level or above.
  • Proven track record leading large-scale transformations within complex, matrixed organizations.
  • Deep experience in organizational adoption for technology-driven transformations, including executive communications and stakeholder readiness.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business strategy into technology requirements, and technology considerations into business recommendations.
  • Strong command of data strategy, taxonomy, metadata governance, and enterprise data management principles.
  • Experience decomposing complex, cross-functional marketing initiatives into clear workstreams, content roadmaps, and operating models.
  • Healthcare, biotech, or pharmaceutical industry experience, with an understanding of medical, legal, and regulatory review processes and HCP and patient engagement requirements.
  • Advanced degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field; MBA or equivalent business education.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through influence in highly matrixed, cross-functional environments and build trust across diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Comfortable operating in fast-moving, ambiguous transformation environments; brings a builder’s mindset and the resilience to sustain momentum across multi-year programs with evolving priorities.
  • Deep understanding of content management systems, customer data platforms, audience segmentation, and marketing automation platforms.
  • Experience enabling offshore or nearshore capability centers in India or similar global enterprise settings.
  • Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to create clear recommendations and decision materials for senior leaders.

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Director, Global Diagnostics Strategy Lead

What you will do

In this vital role, the Director, Global Diagnostic Strategy Lead (DxSL) will lead the creation, alignment, and execution of comprehensive global diagnostic strategies for assigned molecules and programs within a disease area or therapeutic area. The DxSL serves as the primary diagnostic strategy point of contact for program teams and governance forums, helping ensure that diagnostic development plans enable clinical development, regulatory approval, launch, commercialization, and lifecycle management of precision therapeutics.

The Diagnostics (Dx) Group is responsible for the successful transition of biomarker assays into marketed diagnostics that support therapeutic development strategy, regulatory approval, access, and commercialization.

You will:

  • Develop and lead integrated, end-to-end diagnostic strategies from early diagnostic need assessment through launch and lifecycle management.
  • Partner with Product Teams, program leadership and other decision-making forums, to align therapeutic and diagnostic development objectives.
  • Evaluate and propose diagnostic strategic options, including assay and platform approaches, partner strategy, regulatory and commercial pathways, trade-offs, opportunities, costs, timelines, and risks.
  • Lead and oversee Dx Development Teams (DxDTs) to ensure tactical execution of the diagnostic development plan and alignment between Rx and Dx development programs.
  • Influence decision-making in a matrixed environment by communicating balanced, unbiased assessments of diagnostic opportunities and risks.
  • Represent the Dx function with internal stakeholders and external diagnostic development partners.
  • Manage, coach, and develop a small team of Dx technical leads, as applicable, while delivering through cross-functional leadership and influence.

Key Responsibilities

Diagnostic strategy and portfolio leadership

  • Assess the need for diagnostic development for each assigned molecule or program within the disease area or therapeutic area portfolio.
  • Work with cross-functional Dx subject matter experts and program functional leads to build comprehensive, global, long-term diagnostic strategies that support program objectives.
  • Document and communicate diagnostic strategy through appropriate templates, decision materials, and executive-ready slide decks.
  • Provide strategic input to program teams and governance forums to enable informed decisions on diagnostic development options.

Execution through Dx Development Teams

  • Oversee DxDTs to ensure delivery of diagnostic development plans, milestones, timelines, risks, mitigations, and interdependencies.
  • Partner with Project Management to track risks, mitigations, milestones, timelines, resources, and financials across diagnostic development activities.
  • Ensure diagnostic strategies and plans are integrated with therapeutic development plans and clinical trial execution needs.
  • Operate within Amgen governance, policy, and decision-making frameworks, including DAI where applicable.

External partner strategy and business planning

  • Work across Amgen functions to identify, evaluate, and select diagnostic development partners as needed.
  • Oversee partner-selection activities related to diagnostic development, including workplan development and alignment on scope, roles, and deliverables.
  • Lead collaboration with external diagnostic partners to integrate diagnostic development, approval, and launch strategies.

Global launch, commercialization, and lifecycle management

  • Ensure diagnostic strategies incorporate global clinical, regulatory, commercial, access, and regional execution requirements.
  • Partner with global and regional commercial teams to align on commercial diagnostic strategy, including regional or country gap assessments.
  • Lead lifecycle management planning for diagnostic platforms or assays to support program objectives after initial approval and launch.
  • Support diagnostic market landscape assessments and business case development for key strategic choices.

Matrix leadership and stakeholder engagement

  • Communicate effectively with Amgen leadership, therapeutic product teams, cross-functional collaborators, and external partners.
  • Lead with courage and influence without direct authority across a complex matrix environment.
  • Proactively provide balanced and thoughtful input to product teams and other work package teams.
  • Actively seek and incorporate input from Dx Regulatory, Drug Regulatory, Clinical, Medical, Commercial, Value and Access, Business Development, Alliance Management, and other stakeholders.

Core Deliverables

  • Comprehensive diagnostic development strategies for assigned drug development programs and portfolio priorities.
  • Documented Dx strategy materials, including strategy templates, decision documents, and slide decks for cross-functional alignment and governance discussions.
  • Aligned Rx/Dx development plans with clear milestones, risks, mitigations, timelines, and accountabilities.
  • Diagnostic partner selection recommendations and workplans, where partner support is needed.
  • Global and regional diagnostic launch, commercialization, and lifecycle management plans.
  • Dx representation and strategic input at Product Team, EGT, CBDT, DxLT and other relevant forums.

Basic Qualifications

  • Doctorate degree and 4 years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, diagnostics, clinical development, or related experience; OR
  • Master's degree and 8 years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, diagnostics, clinical development, or related experience; OR
  • Bachelor's degree and 10 years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, diagnostics, clinical development, or related experience; AND

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience developing and implementing diagnostic, companion diagnostic, or precision medicine strategies within a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or diagnostics setting.
  • Advanced degree in biomedical sciences, medicine, diagnostics, molecular biology, pathology, genomics, oncology, or related discipline (Ph.D., M.D., Pharm.D., or equivalent).
  • Strong scientific acumen paired with a strategic mindset and the ability to translate biomarker and diagnostic insights into development and commercialization strategies.
  • Knowledge of the clinical, regulatory, commercial, and access considerations that shape global diagnostic development and launch plans.
  • Documented experience with oncology precision medicine, in vitro diagnostics (IVD), companion diagnostics (CDx), biomarker assay development, or diagnostic platform lifecycle management.
  • Experience evaluating diagnostic technologies, development options, market landscapes, and business cases, including trade-offs related to cost, time, risk, opportunity, and global execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence without authority, and gain alignment across senior stakeholders in a matrix environment.
  • Experience working with external diagnostic partners, business development, alliance management, and/or partner governance structures.
  • Familiarity with global regulatory submission requirements and diagnostic evidence expectations across major markets.
  • Experience with clinical trial design, biomarker-driven enrollment or testing strategies, and integration of diagnostic requirements into therapeutic development plans.
  • Excellent executive-level communication, presentation, facilitation, and decision-framing skills.
  • Strong project leadership skills, including resource planning, timeline management, risk identification, risk mitigation, and financial awareness.
  • Learning agility, organizational savvy, self-awareness, adaptability in changing environments, and an organized work style.

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

jobs.description:
Principal Polymer Processing Engineer

Injection Molding

Location: Largo, FL (Remote)
Department: Engineering / Operations
Job Category: Engineering
Career Track: Individual Contributor
Job Profile: Principal Engineer
Reports To: Sr. Director Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
FLSA Status: Exempt

***This position is not eligible for employer-based sponsorship***


Position Summary

The Principal Polymer Processing Engineer is a recognized technical expert responsible for advancing injection molding capabilities, polymer processing technologies, and manufacturing performance across CONMED. This role provides technical leadership for the plastic parts design geometry for injection molding manufacturability; for new injection molds design conceptualization, manufacturing and performance testing; for the plastic injection molding cell equipment selection and performance testing; for the plastic injection molding process optimization and qualification; and for the sustaining support of the plastic injection molding process and mold’s production life cycle maintenance for plastic parts used to manufacture medical devices and components. Working across Engineering, Operations, Quality, R&D, Supply Chain, and external partners, the Principal Polymer Processing Engineer leads highly complex technical initiatives from concept through commercialization and ongoing production. The individual serves as a trusted technical advisor, applying advanced engineering judgment to solve critical processing challenges; establishing technical standards; reducing manufacturing risk; and improving product quality, cost, capacity and reliability.


This is an individual-contributor position that leads through technical expertise, influence, and cross-functional collaboration rather than direct people management.


Key Responsibilities


Technical Leadership and Process Development

  • Serve as a Technical Advisor to Sourcing and Quality in custom molders facilities; molding cells equipment; injection molding process optimization and troubleshooting; mold design and manufacturing; mold preventive maintenance, troubleshooting and tooling engineering; metrology and MSA; and quality engineering technical capacities & capabilities assessment, and periodic audits.
  • Serve as a Subject Matter Expert in part design conceptualization for injection molding manufacturability; injection molding process optimization; injection molding process engineering (troubleshooting); mold design concept optimization; and mold tooling engineering (troubleshooting).
  • Lead the development, optimization, qualification and validation of complex injection molding processes, equipment, molds and supporting technologies.
  • Establish robust processing strategies based on polymer science, material characteristics, part design, mold design, equipment capability, and intended product requirements.
  • Apply scientific molding principles and structured experimentation to define processing windows and ensure repeatable, capable, and controlled manufacturing processes.
  • Provide technical direction for challenging molding applications involving tight tolerances, complex geometries, engineered resins, high-performance polymers, multi-material components, insert molding, overmolding, or other specialized processes.
  • Evaluate emerging polymer-processing technologies and recommend investments that support product innovation, manufacturing capability, capacity, quality, and long-term business needs.
  • Develop and maintain technical standards, engineering practices, design guidelines, specifications, and process-development methodologies.
  • Translate complex technical information into clear recommendations for engineering, operations, and business leadership.

New Product and Technology Development

  • Partner with R&D, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, Operations, and Supply Chain to support new product development and product-transfer activities.
  • Provide design-for-manufacturability guidance related to polymer selection, molded-part design geometry, tooling strategy, tolerances, gating, cooling, shrinkage, warpage, and process capability.
  • Lead or provide technical oversight for mold-flow analysis; tool design reviews; mold manufacturing and performance testing; process characterization; equipment selection and performance testing; and manufacturing-readiness assessments.
  • Identify technical risks early in the development process and establish appropriate mitigation plans.
  • Lead the transition of injection-molded products and processes from development through validation, commercialization, and sustained production.
  • Define critical process parameters and support the development of appropriate inspection, monitoring, and control strategies.
  • Ensure that technical decisions balance product performance, patient and user needs, compliance, manufacturability, cost, capacity, and business continuity.

Process Validation and Compliance

  • Provide technical leadership for mold bench assembly and functional performance assessment; mold installation qualification; molding cell equipment assessment and performance testing; mold dry cycling, mold first out-of-tool and mold functional performance testing; molding process characterization and optimization; plastic forming steel compliance assessment and, if applicable, tweaking (grooming); mold operational qualification; and mold performance qualification activities.
  • Develop or approve technical protocols, reports, engineering studies, acceptance criteria, statistical analyses, and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure polymer-processing activities comply with applicable quality-system requirements, engineering standards, regulatory expectations, and internal procedures.
  • Support risk-management activities, including process FMEAs, design FMEAs, control plans, process-risk assessments, and technical investigations.
  • Partner with Quality Engineering to establish effective process controls and ensure sustained process capability.
  • Provide technical support during internal audits, external audits, regulatory inspections, and customer inquiries, as needed.

Manufacturing and Business Performance

  • Lead the resolution of complex or recurring molding process and/or tooling issues affecting safety, quality, delivery, capacity, cost, or customer service.
  • Apply structured problem-solving methods and advanced data analysis to identify root causes and implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Improve manufacturing performance through cycle-time reduction, scrap reduction, yield improvement, process-capability improvement, automation, tooling optimization, and material utilization.
  • Develop solutions that increase process reliability, reduce variation, and improve overall equipment and operational effectiveness.
  • Assess existing molding equipment, auxiliary systems, tooling, and processes to identify capability gaps, obsolescence risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Support capital-equipment selection, technical justification, supplier evaluation, installation, qualification, and production implementation.
  • Provide technical leadership for design changes, material changes, product transfers, process transfers, supplier transitions, capacity expansion, and manufacturing-network initiatives.
  • Develop business cases and recommendations supported by technical evidence, risk assessment, financial impact, and implementation requirements.

Technical Influence and Collaboration

  • Act as a technical consultant to engineering teams, operations leaders, project teams, and senior leadership.
  • Lead cross-functional technical initiatives that may span multiple products, departments, suppliers, or manufacturing locations.
  • Influence decisions where technical complexity, business risk, or organizational impact is significant.
  • Build effective partnerships with equipment manufacturers, toolmakers, resin suppliers, contract manufacturers, consultants, and other external technical resources.
  • Represent manufacturing and polymer-processing considerations in product, technology, and business-planning discussions.
  • Facilitate technical reviews and ensure decisions, actions, risks, and accountabilities are clearly documented.
  • Communicate effectively with technical and nontechnical audiences at all levels of the organization.

Knowledge Development and Mentoring

  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to engineers, technicians, molders, and other manufacturing professionals.
  • Build organizational capability by sharing specialized knowledge, developing technical training, and establishing repeatable engineering methods.
  • Review and provide guidance on the technical work of other engineers without serving as their direct manager.
  • Promote disciplined experimentation, fact-based decision making, continuous improvement, and strong engineering practices.
  • Maintain current knowledge of developments in polymer science, molding technology, manufacturing systems, medical-device requirements, and industry best practices.
  • Contribute to the development of CONMED’s long-term polymer-processing and manufacturing-technology roadmap.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Polymer Engineering, Plastics Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Science, or closely related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible engineering experience involving injection molding, polymer processing, plastics manufacturing, tooling, or closely related manufacturing technologies.
  • 2 years of experience applying technical knowledge and expertise troubleshooting injection molded parts noncompliance opportunities to determine whether root cause is part design geometry, raw material, raw material handling, molding process, mold steel dimensions, mold steel wear, mold design conceptualization, molding cell selection, molding cell functional performance, part’s inspection method, inspection fixture, inspection equipment, parts conveying, parts packaging design, parts storing and/or part’s transit related.
  • 2 years of experience leading complex technical projects and influencing decisions across multiple functions. Experience developing or reviewing engineering protocols, validation documents, technical reports, specifications, risk assessments, and process documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or doctorate in Polymer Engineering, Plastics Engineering, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline.

jobs.excerpt: This project proposes a real-time workflow for 3D X-ray ptychography that uses a sample-specific surrogate model to reduce reconstruction time.
jobs.description:
This project proposes a real-time workflow for 3D X-ray ptychography that uses a sample-specific surrogate model to reduce reconstruction time. In 3D ptychography, a sample is illuminated from many angles, and a 2D image is recovered for each angle with iterative phase retrieval (e.g., ePIE) before the images are combined into a 3D volume. Because the phase retrieval is repeated for every direction, it dominates the total runtime. Earlier surrogate-model studies sped up this step but did not evaluate the whole workflow, and they typically required a training dataset prepared in advance. The proposed method instead builds the surrogate model on-the-fly. First, directional subsampling selects a subset of the projection angles. ePIE is run only on those angles, and the resulting diffraction pattern and object image pairs form a small training set. A surrogate model is trained on this set and predicts initial object estimates for the remaining angles. After preprocessing, these predictions initialize a second ePIE pass. The workflow will run on GPUs. Additional work will include the development of a foundation surrogate model for diverse samples and testing other surrogate architectures.

The company's first FDA-approved product is REVTORPYK (gedatolisib), a potent, pan-PI3K and mTORC1/2 inhibitor that comprehensively blockades the PAM pathway. REVTORPYK is approved to treat adults with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer that progressed on prior endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting.

The Phase 3 VIKTORIA-2 trial is evaluating gedatolisib in combination with palbociclib and either fulvestrant or letrozole for the first-line treatment of HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer. About Us
Our company is on a mission to reduce food waste and make high-quality, affordable food accessible to everyone. Through our innovative app-based marketplace, we connect shoppers with discounted perishable items while helping retailers turn would-be waste into revenue and meaningful environmental impact. We’re growing quickly across North America and partnering with retailers of all sizes to expand our reach.

If you’re passionate about creating real change for people and the planet, we’d love for you to join us. Your work here will directly contribute to a mission that helps families save money, reduces waste, and builds a more sustainable future.

The Role and Context

Flashfood is the app for grocery's best deals. We partner with leading grocery retailers across North America to sell fresh food nearing its best-by date at a discount, helping shoppers save money while preventing good food from going to waste.

We help drive incremental revenue, improve shrink outcomes, increase basket size, and deepen customer loyalty, all while advancing sustainability goals.

As we expand into larger and more complex enterprise organizations, we are hiring a Sales Director to lead that expansion. Someone who understands the grocery ecosystem deeply, carries genuine executive presence, and has a track record of closing with major enterprise retailers.

As Sales Director, you will own strategic, enterprise-level sales with large, multi-banner grocery retailers across the US. This is a senior individual-contributor leadership role: you will run full-cycle enterprise sales while also helping shape Flashfood's sales strategy, process, and culture as we scale into our next tier of partnerships.

This role is not transactional and is not an entry point into enterprise sales. It requires, as hard requirements:

  • Deep, credible knowledge of how grocery organizations actually operate: merchandising, operations, shrink, and store execution
  • Executive presence that reads as credible the moment you're in front of a C-suite or VP-level audience
  • A demonstrated, verifiable history of closing complex deals with major enterprise retailers
  • Comfort leading long, multi-threaded sales cycles involving procurement, legal, and data security stakeholders
  • The ability to think beyond features and build executive-level, financially grounded business cases
  • Deep grocery connections with leading grocers across the Midwest region, especially in Michigan, Ohio, Illinois, Indiana, and Pennsylvania.

You will own the full sales cycle, from market strategy and executive engagement through negotiation and close, and will partner with leadership to influence how Flashfood's enterprise motion evolves.

What You'll Do

Strategic Enterprise Development

  • Identify and prioritize high-value grocery targets across your territory
  • Develop account penetration strategies tailored to each organization's structure, priorities, and economics
  • Map buying committees across operations, merchandising, finance, digital, sustainability, and executive leadership
  • Build and sustain multi-threaded, executive-level relationships within complex retail organizations

Industry-Led, Executive Sales Execution

  • Lead discovery grounded in real grocery operational challenges (shrink, labor constraints, margin pressure, inventory management, digital engagement)
  • Translate retailer pain points into quantifiable, board-ready business cases
  • Position Flashfood as a strategic lever for enterprise performance, not solely a shrink too
  • Develop and deliver executive-ready proposals with clear ROI, financial modeling, and rollout plans, directly to VP and C-suite audiences

Complex Deal Leadership & Close

  • Drive long, multi-region sales cycles with discipline and clarity
  • Navigate procurement, legal, data security, and operational stakeholders
  • Structure enterprise agreements that support scalable, long-term partnerships
  • Independently close large, multi-region or enterprise-wide deals with major grocery retailers

    Sales Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence
  • Help define and refine Flashfood's enterprise sales process, playbooks, and culture as the team scales
  • Partner closely with Marketing, Product, Implementation, and Customer Success to align enterprise strategy
  • Bring structured, executive-level feedback from the field to inform product and go-to-market decisions
  • Maintain disciplined CRM hygiene, forecasting accuracy, and pipeline management

What You’ll Bring

Deeply Connected in Grocery (Required)

  • Extensive experience inside, or selling into, large grocery retailers
  • Fluent in the internal dynamics of merchandising, operations, and store execution
  • An existing network of C-suite and VP-level decision-makers across regional or national grocery chains

Strategic Thinker

  • You think beyond immediate deals to enterprise-wide rollout and long-term value creation
  • You connect operational improvements directly to financial outcomes
  • You build executive-level narratives grounded in data, not just product features

Proven Enterprise Closer (Required)

  • 10+ years of enterprise sales experience, with strong preference for grocery retail, CPG-tech, retail-tech, or adjacent sectors
  • Demonstrated, referenceable success closing complex, six- and seven-figure deals with major enterprise retailers
  • A consistent history of meeting or exceeding quota at a senior/Director level

Operator in Challenging Environments

  • Experience selling in markets with long cycles and multiple stakeholders
  • You maintain momentum and pipeline discipline even when deals stall
  • You operate with resilience, ownership, and executive-level judgment

Executive Presence (Required)

  • Command credibility the moment you're in a room with senior retail executives
  • Polished, confident communicator, equally strong in written and verbal executive settings
  • Skilled, composed negotiator of complex, multi-year enterprise contracts
  • Comfortable building and presenting financial models and ROI narratives directly to C-suite stakeholders

What Sets This Role Apart

This is a high-impact, high-visibility role with direct influence on company growth and on how Flashfood's enterprise sales function is built. We are looking for someone who:

  • Brings instant credibility the moment they walk into a grocery boardroom
  • Speaks the language of retail operators fluently
  • Has already proven they can close with major enterprise retailers
  • Is motivated by performance, ownership, and mission
  • Wants to help define a category-leading sales function, not just carry a number

What We Offer

  • Performance-driven compensation aligned with enterprise impact
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits
  • 100% remote
  • Learning & development budget
  • A defining, senior-level role in scaling a mission-driven company into its next stage of enterprise growth

Our Mission

Flashfood exists to reduce food waste at scale while helping families save on groceries. We partner with retailers to unlock value from inventory that would otherwise go unsold, benefiting shoppers, stores, and the planet.

If you understand grocery deeply, carry real executive presence, have closed with major enterprise retailers before, and want to drive meaningful growth, we would love to connect.

Flashfood is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences, and we’re dedicated to creating an environment where everyone feels supported and empowered to do their best work.

Job Description Summary


This position can be based remotely anywhere in the U.S. (there may be some restrictions based on legal entity). Please note that this role would not provide relocation as a result. Job description summary

The Data Innovation, Partnerships and Products (DIPP) team sits within the Data Products and Foundations pillar of SPT and is focused on enabling trusted, scalable data access and partnerships that support improved decision-making across Novartis.

The Director, MAPS (Market Access, Patient Services) and Medical Data Partnerships Lead will play a critical role in establishing and managing strategic data partnerships that support the US Commercial organization and broader SPT priorities.

This position will be responsible for overseeing Novartis’s existing strategic data partnerships within DIPP to ensure compliance and quality are maintained and that Novartis teams have the appropriate systems, processes, and data access to meet business needs.

As the Director, MAPS and Medical Data Partnerships Lead, this role will focus on managing external data partnerships, monitoring spend, and ensuring that partnerships meet data needs, established data standards, governance expectations, and regulatory requirements. The role will collaborate with cross-functional teams to assess partnership effectiveness, track partnership performance and spend, enforce data stewardship practices, and ensure data assets are leveraged effectively across the organization.

The role will also help identify new and innovative data offerings and evaluate where AI can be responsibly integrated into partnership models, data workflows, and commercial use cases to improve speed, in-sight generation, and enterprise value.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Oversee the performance and outcomes of external data partnerships, including third-party platforms, vendors, and technology solutions
  • Develop and execute the organization’s data partnership strategy, including the identification of the organization’s critical data needs
  • Partner with Medical, Market Access, and Patient Services stakeholders to identify, evaluate, and manage external data partnerships that strengthen medical insights, real-world evidence, access, patient services, field medical execution, and outcomes-oriented decision-making
  • Work collaboratively to ensure data is addressing use cases Identify and evaluate innovative data offerings in collaboration with the Innovative Data Offerings team, emerging data sources, and opportunities to integrate AI-enabled capabilities that enhance customer engagement, marketing effectiveness, decision-making, and scalable business impact
  • Establish data quality SLAs and metrics with external data partners to ensure high quality data remains available for Novartis teams
  • Working with Data Monitoring and Standards, monitor and enforce data quality, security, and compliance standards for all external data sources, platforms, and vendors, ensuring adherence to regulatory requirements and internal policies for data management
  • Work collaboratively with data vendors and cross-functional teams to address data quality issues and communicate any corresponding changes
  • Facilitate acquisition of data from requirements gathering through integration into Novartis’s platforms and systems
  • Establish oversight mechanisms for external data partnerships, ensuring compliance with data standards, data-sharing agreements, and internal policies for data management
  • Support the implementation of data stewardship practices across platforms, vendors, and technology solutions, to verify data is properly managed and governed throughout the partnership, providing performance metrics and governance reports to senior leadership
  • Coordinate training and awareness initiatives with internal teams around best practices to promote effective and compliant data usage
  • Continuously evaluate existing partnerships and technology solutions to ensure standards across the broader set of DIPP data partnerships are maintained

Novartis seeks an individual with extensive experience in establishing and managing data partnerships. The ideal candidate will have a deep understanding of the data partnership landscape, including industry best practices for collaborating with external data providers. Experience working for a data vendor or working extensively with functional or therapeutic area data is highly desirable, particularly where that experience includes translating business needs into data requirements and ensuring data can be effectively integrated, governed, and used. A proven ability to navigate data-related risks—such as privacy, security, and compliance issues—while building mutually beneficial partnerships is essential. The successful candidate will be committed to driving continuous improvement in the organization’s data partnership strategy, leveraging data insights and industry trends to strengthen collaboration and maximize the value of external data assets.

The ideal candidate should also bring curiosity and practical experience evaluating emerging data capabilities, including AI-enabled tools, advanced analytics opportunities, and new partnership models that can expand how data is accessed, integrated, and applied across the business.

Essential Requirements:

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Business Administration, or related field
  • Minimum 8+ years of experience in establishing and managing data partnerships, with a strong focus on data governance, data management, or related roles
  • Expert understanding of data partnership principles, frameworks, and best practices, with a proven ability to forge strategic collaborations with external data providers and vendors
  • Preferred experience working for a data vendor or partnering extensively with data vendors, functional teams, or therapeutic area teams to define, evaluate, integrate, and operationalize data assets
  • Familiarity with regulatory requirements and industry standards related to data privacy and security
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills
  • Ability to influence and drive change in a complex organizational environment
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess and manage risks associated with external data partnerships, ensuring the integrity, security, and quality of shared data
