jobs.title: Claims Manager
jobs.excerpt: At Fix Network, we build highways of connections!
jobs.description:
At Fix Network, we build highways of connections!

Our story began in 1992 with the founding of Fix Auto Collision in Quebec, Canada. Fix Network is the fastest growing automotive aftermarket service provider in the world, with over 2,000 shops in 21 countries. As we expand our business footprint around the world, we are always looking for dynamic people to keep Fix Network in a leadership position. This is an exciting time for Fix Network and we need people with great adaptability to be part of our incredible team!

Step on the gas and explore the exciting daily road of a Claims Manager at Fix Network !

Fix Network is looking for a Claims Manager who loves to put the foot to the floor!

In this role, you will be responsible for delivering exceptional customer service while managing automotive glass claims in accordance with company policies, insurer requirements. This role is responsible for reviewing and processing claims, responding to inbound queue calls, resolving claim-related inquiries, and ensuring the accuracy and completeness of claim documentation.

The daily road of a Claims Manager at Fix Network

  • Manage automobile glass claims from receipt through resolution in accordance with company policies, insurer and requirements.
  • Review and validate invoices, supporting documentation, and claim details to ensure accuracy and compliance with insurer pricing agreements and program requirements.
  • Verify vehicle information, parts, labour, and supporting documentation before approving claims.
  • Respond to inbound queue calls from customers and participating repair facilities in a professional, courteous, and timely manner, providing claim updates, answering inquiries, and resolving issues whenever possible.
  • Communicate with glass repair facilities, insurance partners, and internal stakeholders to resolve claim discrepancies and outstanding issues.
  • Investigate and resolve claim exceptions, billing discrepancies, and documentation deficiencies.
  • Ensure all claims are processed in accordance with Québec regulations and AMF licensing requirements.
  • Maintain accurate claim records and update internal systems with all relevant claim information.
  • Monitor claims to ensure timely processing and resolution while meeting established service standards.
  • Respond to inquiries from repair facilities and insurance partners in a professional and timely manner.
  • Identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities to improve claims processes and operational efficiency.
  • Stay informed of insurer requirements, pricing agreements, and industry best practices related to automotive glass claims.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

The pilot we are looking for :

  • Valid Insurance Adjuster License
  • 3-5 years of experience handling automotive glass claims, insurance claims, or claims adjudication.
  • Bilingualism (French and English) is mandatory as the Claims Manager will be working with insurers across Canada and will respond to claims in both French and English.
  • Knowledge of automotive glass repair and replacement procedures.
  • Understanding of insurer billing practices and pricing agreements.
  • Strong attention to detail and analytical skills.
  • Excellent customer service and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple claims in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with claims management systems and Microsoft Office.

Why Fix network ?

In addition to joining dynamic and highly motivated team in a flexible and constantly evolving work environment. You will have access to the following benefits:
Why Join Fix Network?

  • 3 weeks of vacation from day one, plus 5 sick days per year.
  • An employer RRSP contribution matching 50% of your contributions, up to a maximum of 3% of your salary.
  • Group benefits with 75% of premiums paid by the employer, including telemedicine services.
  • Up to $3,000 per year in tuition reimbursement to support your professional development.
  • An annual $250 allowance to spend in our Fix Network apparel and merchandise store.
  • A referral bonus of up to $1,000 when you help us find our next great talent.
  • Opportunities to connect and celebrate throughout the year, including monthly celebrations to welcome new employees and recognize birthdays, service anniversaries, promotions, and other milestones, as well as our summer BBQ, holiday party, and other team events.
  • Our annual Team Meeting, bringing together team members from around the world for several days to align on company priorities, connect with international colleagues, and enjoy valuable team-building experiences.
  • Free on-site parking.

jobs.description:
Digital Services Manager

Description -

Head of Digital Services, U.S. Channel


Job Description

Role Overview

The Head of Digital Services, U.S. Channel is responsible for leading HP’s Partner Development Manager (PDM) team and scaling HP’s digital software and services business across the U.S. partner ecosystem. This leader owns the strategy, go-to-market execution, partner practice development, and revenue performance required to position Digital Employee Experience (DEX) as a core channel growth pillar and transform the partner motion from hardware-led transactions to outcome-based, recurring experience-led services.


The role acts as the senior architect for HP’s DEX-led partner services motion, defining how partners assess, sell, deploy, optimize, secure, and renew digital experience solutions around HP’s portfolio. The Head of Digital Services will align HP sales, product, services, finance, operations, marketing, and program teams behind a scalable partner activation model while ensuring the PDM team is equipped to build partner capability, drive adoption, and deliver measurable recurring revenue growth.


Key Responsibilities

Lead the Partner Development Manager Team

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Partner Development Managers accountable for partner practice development, pipeline creation, deal execution support, account planning, competitive positioning, and revenue growth in HP digital services.
  • Establish the PDM operating rhythm, including forecasting discipline, partner prioritization, pipeline inspection, business reviews, KPI tracking, and executive reporting.
  • Ensure PDMs operate as category and services specialists who build partner capability, contribute to joint business planning, and help partners become self-sufficient in selling and delivering HP-based services.
  • Set clear engagement boundaries and collaboration models with PBMs, DBMs, end-user sellers, technical consultants, product teams, and services specialists.

Build and Scale DEX-Led Partner Practices

  • Define the end-to-end blueprint partners use to launch and scale HP-based DEX practices, including assessment offers, adoption services, optimization motions, security adjacencies, service catalogs, pricing and margin models, delivery playbooks, onboarding, QBR cadence, renewals, and expansion motions.
  • Develop a DEX maturity model that guides partners from assess, deploy, and adopt through monitor, optimize, automate, secure, and expand.
  • Build partner business cases that quantify service margin, investment requirements, time-to-first-revenue, delivery capacity, customer productivity impact, and customer lifetime value.
  • Pair partner practice plans with specialty pricing, commitment-based programs, MDF, incentives, certification, and enablement structures that reward adoption, outcomes, renewals, and recurring revenue.

Drive Digital Services Growth Across the Channel

  • Position digital services as a core growth pillar of the U.S. Channel and a strategic revenue engine, not a hardware attach motion.
  • Scale annual recurring revenue through DEX-led partner offers, subscription motions, consumption models, adoption services, optimization engagements, and expansion plays.
  • Activate VAR, distribution, strategic partner, digital workplace, end-user computing, and security routes to market with clear value propositions, economic models, sales plays, and partner-ready DEX offers.
  • Use data, dashboards, market insights, and partner feedback to identify growth opportunities, prioritize partner investments, and improve services penetration.

Advance Solution Integration and Practice Specialization

  • Enable partners to monetize HP Workforce Experience Platform capabilities, including fleet analytics, experience scoring, operational intelligence, workflow automation, and continuous optimization services.
  • Integrate Digital Employee Experience capabilities into partner offerings, including endpoint analytics, device performance telemetry, sentiment insight, and AI-driven remediation.
  • Embed HP Security into DEX-led partner offerings as an important layer of endpoint resilience, risk reduction, compliance awareness, and proactive experience management.
  • Ensure the PDM team translates HP portfolio priorities into partner-specific practice roadmaps, enablement plans, and revenue-producing offers.

Develop the DEX and Security Partner Ecosystem

  • Recruit, activate, and scale partners with the technical, operational, and commercial capability to deliver DEX-led services around HP’s digital portfolio.
  • Prioritize partners with existing digital workplace, endpoint management, employee experience, ITSM, security operations, and end-user computing practices to shorten time-to-revenue.
  • Define security-adjacent DEX routes to market across endpoint security visibility, risk posture awareness, compliance reporting, proactive remediation, and experience-driven operational intelligence.
  • Establish integration points between HP telemetry, partner service desks, experience analytics, automation workflows, security tooling, and recurring commercial models for monitoring, optimization, and compliance-oriented services.

Influence Internal Strategy, Programs, and Operating Models

  • Serve as the internal champion for digital services across HP, building executive sponsorship and organizational alignment for the channel services business.
  • Translate partner wins, customer outcomes, competitive dynamics, and market signals into business requirements for product roadmap, pricing, programs, tools, support, and operational processes.
  • Advocate for the technical resources required to scale DEX-led partner practices, including DEX specialists, technical consultants, solution architects, security subject-matter experts, and pre-sales engineering support.
  • Drive requirements for SKU simplification, quoting, ordering, provisioning, entitlement management, renewals, deal registration, funnel visibility, and reporting.

Required Experience and Qualifications

  • Proven success leading channel, partner development, services, software, digital workplace, employee experience, endpoint management, or security-adjacent organizations in a complex technology environment.
  • Deep understanding of the Digital Employee Experience market, including endpoint analytics, experience scoring, sentiment insight, automation, remediation, ITSM integration, adoption services, and recurring revenue motions.
  • Background in security, endpoint resilience, risk management, or security operations is strongly preferred; experience with major DEX market players such as Nexthink, Lakeside, ControlUp, 1E, or similar platforms is a plus.
  • The ideal candidate will bring experience from a leading DEX competitor or a proven track record of building and scaling a software or digital services practice within a hardware company.
  • Experience building partner practices, scaling partner capability, launching new offers, and translating portfolio strategy into field execution.
  • Strong executive presence with the ability to influence across sales, category, product, services, finance, operations, marketing, and partner leadership teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to use data, market insight, and partner feedback to shape strategy, prioritize investments, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
  • Track record of building high-performing teams, coaching specialist sellers or partner development resources, and establishing disciplined operating rhythms.

Leadership Attributes

  • Transformational leader who can move the channel from transactional selling to outcome-based, services-led growth.
  • Strategic operator who converts vision into scalable operating models, clear ownership, and measurable execution.
  • Partner-first executive who understands how partners make money, where they invest, and what capabilities they need to scale.
  • Strong collaborator who can orchestrate across HP and remove friction for partners and field teams.
  • Commercially disciplined leader who balances growth, profitability, adoption, renewal, and long-term partner health.

Success Metrics

Category

Revenue

Digital services revenue growth, ARR attainment, YoY growth, services mix, and partner-delivered recurring revenue

Practice building

DEX-focused partners recruited, activated, certified, and revenue-producing

Adoption

Software attach rate, active seats, deployment-to-adoption conversion, experience improvement, and utilization of DEX-led partner services

Retention

Renewal rate, net expansion, churn reduction, and customer retention through partner-led services

Partner health

Service margin, practice profitability, partner investment, certification progress, DEX capability growth, and partner-delivered recurring services revenue

Internal impact

Pricing, program, process, support, and roadmap requirements adopted by HP stakeholder teams

Customer impact

Improved experience outcomes, satisfaction, reference-ability, and measurable value delivered through HP digital services

Role - Video Editor(AI & Ads) - Tamil

About Lokal : In 2018, we began with a WhatsApp group with a simple hypothesis: people in tier-2/3 towns weren’t really using the internet meaningfully yet. We believed that if we started with local content in their own language, they’d come back every day; once there was a habit and trust, that same space could naturally grow into classifieds and, eventually, something they used for almost everything online. This spark became Lokal. Our first instinct was to put everything in one place & one app - local updates, classifieds, jobs, matrimony and more. It worked, till it stopped working. Users gave us the insight - when one use case outweighs the others, everything else seems like noise. We listened. Like how Craigslist quietly seeded a generation of focused companies & marketplaces, we began unbundling and verticalising. Today, Lokal is a house of focused apps, many products, one mission: to connect Tier-2/3+ India to the Knowledge, opportunities, tools, and experts they’ve always deserved.

We now operate dozens of live apps across categories like:

  • Edutainment & Skill Learning – practical skills and learning in regional languages (GyanTV)
  • Matrimonial Matchmaking – hyperlocal, compatibility-first partner search (Lokal Matrimony)
  • Agri Consulting – farmer-first advisory in local languages (AgriLokal)
  • Local Jobs – blue- and grey-collar opportunities close to home (Lokal Jobs, Sahi Jobs)
  • Social & Community – a place to find & post social updates (Lokal app)
  • Emotional Well-being & Peer Support – safe spaces to talk and feel heard (Dostt & Eaze)
  • Astrology & Guidance – instant access to trusted Astrologers via chat and voice (AstroLokal) Advisory Services – early bets in legal help, financial guidance, career counselling, and more

Under the hood, Lokal is a discovery and access platform: local-language internet + deep Bharat insight+ AI. When someone opens a product we’ve built, they don’t wade through clutter; they get a straight line to what they came for.

This is the story new teammates walk into: a company that started as a WhatsApp group, became a family of focused apps, and kept one belief at the centre — access changes lives.

We ship fast. We learn fast. We build for Bharat.

We are backed by leading global and domestic investors including Y Combinator, Sony, Global Brain, India Quotient, and 3one4 Capital.

Interested? Click here to apply now!

 

About the Role:

At TELUS Digital, we are advancing the future of Artificial Intelligence by helping AI systems understand, process, and generate human speech with greater accuracy and naturalness.

As an AI Speech & Audio Specialist in our AI Community, you will contribute to the development and improvement of next-generation speech AI technologies, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Text-to-Speech (TTS), Voice AI, and audio machine learning systems.

We rely on our global community of specialists to evaluate, create, refine, and improve high-quality speech and audio datasets. Your expertise in audio production, speech analysis, linguistics, or voice technology will help ensure AI models deliver natural, accurate, culturally relevant, and human-like voice experiences.

At TELUS Digital, you will play a key role in shaping how AI listens, understands, and communicates with people around the world.

 

Key Responsibilities:

·         Evaluate AI-generated speech (TTS) for naturalness, pronunciation accuracy, rhythm, tone, emotion, and overall voice quality.

·         Review and improve speech recognition outputs (ASR) by identifying transcription errors, pronunciation issues, accents, and linguistic nuances.

·         Perform professional audio editing tasks including segmentation, trimming, noise reduction, silence adjustment, and quality enhancement.

·         Analyze audio recordings using waveform and spectrogram-based tools to identify quality issues.

·         Support the creation and validation of high-quality speech datasets used for AI model training and evaluation.

·         Review voice recordings for clarity, consistency, articulation, and technical quality.

·         Perform audio quality checks including loudness levels, background noise detection, clipping, distortion, and export specifications.

·         Support voice AI projects including TTS, ASR, voice generation, voice similarity, voice mimicry, and conversational AI evaluation.

·         Apply expertise in phonetics, linguistics, audio engineering, or speech technology to improve AI-generated voice experiences.

 

Qualification path

Mandatory Qualifications:

Education / Professional Background:

Minimum of one of the following:

·         Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in:

·         Audio Engineering

·         Sound Engineering

·         Music Technology

·         Linguistics

·         Phonetics

·         Speech-Language Pathology

·         Computational Linguistics

·         Computer Science (Speech/AI focus)

·         Related audio or speech fields

 

OR

Professional experience in:

 

·         Audio production

·         Sound design

·         Dialogue editing

·         Voice recording

·         Podcast/audio post-production

·         Speech data creation

·         AI speech projects

·         Technical Experience:

·         Experience with at least one professional audio tool:

·         Adobe Audition

·         iZotope RX

·         Pro Tools

·         Reaper

·         Audacity

·         Logic Pro

·         Cubase

·         Other Digital Audio Workstations (DAWs)

 

Knowledge of:

·         Audio editing and restoration

·         Noise reduction

·         Speech segmentation

·         Spectrogram analysis

·         Audio quality assessment

·         Voice/audio processing workflows

Language Requirements:

·         Native-level proficiency (C1/C2+) in the required language is preferred for language-specific projects.

·         Ability to identify pronunciation, accent, and linguistic nuances.

·         English proficiency sufficient to understand technical instructions and project guidelines.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with:

·         Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)

·         Text-to-Speech (TTS)

·         Voice AI

·         Speech datasets

·         Audio annotation

·         Voice cloning or voice mimicry projects

·         ADR / dubbing

·         Localization audio

·         Broadcast or media production

·         AI model evaluation

 

Assessment:

·         To join the TELUS Digital AI Community, candidates will complete:

·         Subject-specific qualification assessment

·         Practical audio/speech evaluation (where applicable)

·         Identity verification process

 

The assessment may include:

 

·         Audio quality evaluation

·         Speech recognition review

·         Audio editing tasks

·         Voice quality analysis

·         Linguistic accuracy evaluation

 

Payment:

Currently, pay rates for specialists range from $6 - $40 USD per hour depending on expertise, project complexity, and market requirements. *Location and language is directly dependent.

Payment terms and rates are defined separately for each project engagement.

Why Join the TELUS Digital AI Community:

·         Community Connection: Work remotely as part of a 1M+ diverse global AI Community of contributors and experts.

·         Impactful Expertise: Use your native language and academic degree to shape real-world AI systems and products used by millions every day.

·         Hands-on Innovation: Gain experience in the latest AI research, evaluation, and fine-tuning methodologies.

·         Global Collaboration: Collaborate with a network of specialists across 20+ domains and 500+ languages and dialects.

·         Flexible Engagement: Manage your own schedule while making a meaningful impact on the future of technology.

 

TELUS Digital AI Community

Our global AI Community is a vibrant network of more than one million contributors from diverse backgrounds who help customers collect, enhance, train, translate, and localize content to build better AI models. Become part of our growing community and contribute to the development of innovative AI technologies used by some of the world's largest brands.

 

Independent Contractor Relationship:

This opportunity is offered on an independent contractor basis. Contributors have the flexibility to choose when and how much they work, subject to project availability and quality requirements. jobs.title: Sales Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About MonteraAt Montera, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure.
jobs.description:
About Montera

At Montera, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Founder-led with $1.5B backed by Stonepeak, Montera is driven by a future-focused vision: to develop and operate hyperscale data centers essential for tomorrow's technology. Our mission is to deliver strategically located, hyperscale data centers designed for speed, reliability, and scalability. Backed by decades of experience in design, construction, and operations, we don’t just build—we execute with purpose.

Our Values

  • Client First Alignment: We align every solution to our clients’ goals.
  • Speed with Certainty: Velocity matters. We deliver with urgency and precision.
  • Operational Excellence: Decades of experience drive our high standards.
  • Safety & Integrity: Safety is non-negotiable. We lead with integrity and transparency.
  • Ownership Mentality: We think like owners, because we are.

The Opportunity

Montera is seeking a Principal Sales Engineer — the client-facing engineering authority for our sales activity with hyperscalers and AI-native cloud and model providers. Sitting in the Product team and reporting to the CTO, this role bridges outside sales and internal design: it partners directly with the SVP of Business Development & Hyperscale Accounts, who owns the commercial relationship and pursuit strategy, while the Principal Sales Engineer owns technical credibility in the room.

This is a senior individual-contributor role within Montera's Principal Engineering & Architecture Leadership family. You'll present Montera's reference designs, power and cooling approach, delivery model, and campus capabilities to customer engineering, infrastructure, real estate, and procurement teams — translating customer requirements into terms the design team can act on, and design and delivery constraints into terms customers and the sales team can act on. The role also requires fluency in how hyperscale campuses are financed and governed: Montera's assets are backed by private-equity sponsors and lenders, customer commitments must hold up to lender and investment-committee diligence, and multi-customer campuses may be governed through condominium or owners'-association structures that directly shape site design, metering, access, and expansion rights.

What You’ll Do

  • Serve as technical lead on assigned hyperscaler and AI-native customer pursuits — supporting the SVP of Business Development across the full sales cycle, from first meeting through contract, including site tours, design workshops, and RFS/schedule reviews.
  • Present Montera's campus designs, power and cooling architectures, interconnection strategy, and delivery schedule to customer executives and technical teams, and represent Montera credibly at industry conferences, customer forums, and standards groups.
  • Run structured discovery on customer capacity ramps, rack and power density, liquid cooling, resilience tiers, network and fiber needs, security posture, and sustainability commitments — mapping requirements to Montera reference architectures and documenting gaps, deviations, and cost/schedule consequences before commitments are made.
  • Partner with the VP, Data Center Design and the Principal Architect, Electrical, Mechanical, Controls, and Network leads to scope customer-specific modifications and confirm they are deliverable; feed market and customer intelligence back into product strategy and reference-design evolution.
  • Own the technical content of RFIs, RFPs, and customer technical diligence — coordinating design, development, delivery, and operations into consistent, accurate responses, and preparing technical exhibits (specifications, SLAs, delivery milestones, responsibility matrices) that support lease and contract negotiation.
  • Ensure customer-facing technical positions are bankable — consistent with what lenders, equity sponsors, and independent engineers will test — and support PE sponsor, lender, and technical-advisor diligence sessions.
  • Advise sales and design on how multi-customer campus structures (including condominium or owners'-association governance) affect site design: demarcation, shared vs. dedicated utilities, interconnection and substation ownership, metering, access zoning, and phased expansion rights — reflecting those constraints in master plans before they reach customers.
  • Act as the voice of the customer within the Product team, and report pursuit status, technical risks, and open decisions to the CTO and the SVP of Business Development on a regular cadence.

Requirements

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Mechanical, or a related engineering discipline; advanced degree or PE licensure preferred.
  • 12+ years in data center or mission-critical infrastructure, including 5+ years in a customer-facing sales/solutions engineering or pre-sales technical role at a hyperscale colocation provider, developer, or hyperscaler.
  • Direct experience supporting hyperscale or AI customer pursuits through RFP, technical diligence, and contract negotiation — including multi-megawatt, multi-building campuses.
  • Strong command of data center power, cooling, and network systems at hyperscale — including high-density and liquid-cooled AI environments — and how those systems drive cost, schedule, and availability.
  • Working understanding of how campuses are financed and held: PE sponsor and lender diligence, independent-engineer review, and how multi-tenant governance (condominium / owners'-association structures) affects site design and expansion.
  • Exceptional presentation skills, with a record of presenting to customer executives and technical committees and simplifying complex subjects without losing accuracy.
  • An established network among hyperscaler and AI-infrastructure engineering, real estate, and procurement teams — and the credibility to open and sustain those relationships.
  • Sound commercial judgment, discipline around confidentiality, and the ability to say clearly what Montera can and cannot commit to.
  • Preferred: experience at a hyperscale colocation/wholesale developer or on the customer side; familiarity with utility interconnection and flexible-load arrangements, $/W and yield-on-cost modeling, hyperscale lease exhibits, and presenting to lenders, rating agencies, or investment committees.
    •

Benefits

Why Join Montera?

At Montera, you’ll shape the next generation of digital infrastructure while being supported by a team that values integrity, collaboration, and long-term partnership. We’re a remote-first company that empowers our people with flexibility, ownership, and meaningful rewards.

Compensation:

At Montera, we believe great work starts with investing in great people. That is why we offer a competitive and thoughtful total compensation package designed to recognize the value each team member brings.

Our compensation ranges are informed by market data and aligned to job level and role. When making hiring and compensation decisions, we consider a variety of factors, including skills, experience, education, training, competencies, and overall business needs.

The reasonable compensation range for this role is $175,000 - $225,000 per year.

About the Client

We're helping a growing AI and process automation consultancy based in Munich, Germany find a Senior AI Automation Engineer to design and deliver sophisticated automation and AI-powered business solutions.

The company works with small and medium-sized businesses across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, helping them streamline operations, improve efficiency, and scale through intelligent automation. Its solutions span CRM systems, AI agents, automated workflows, business intelligence, and custom software integrations.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior AI Automation Engineer who combines a strong software development background with advanced hands-on experience in automation engineering and AI integrations.

You'll design and build complex automation systems, integrate AI technologies, develop custom code, and create tailored software solutions when existing platforms aren't sufficient.

Working closely with the founder and delivery team, you'll take ownership of projects from requirements gathering and technical design through development, deployment, and optimization.

This isn't a role for someone who only builds simple automations. We're looking for a software engineer who understands system architecture, can solve complex technical challenges, and knows when to use low-code platforms versus custom development.

Role Details

Commitment: Full-Time (40 hours/week)
Working Hours: CET
Location: Fully Remote
Engagement: Independent Contractor
Monthly Rate: $1,800-$2,400 (can be higher, depending on level of experience)

What You'll Do

AI Automation & Workflow Development

  • Design, build, and maintain complex automation workflows using n8n, Make.com, and Zapier.

  • Develop end-to-end integrations connecting business applications, APIs, databases, CRMs, and AI models.

  • Build and optimize HubSpot CRM automations, including contacts, deals, pipelines, properties, and workflows.

  • Develop AI-powered solutions and agents for sales, research, customer support, and other business processes.

  • Troubleshoot and optimize workflows for reliability, scalability, and maintainability.

Software Development & AI Systems

  • Develop custom integrations, scripts, and applications using JavaScript/TypeScript and/or Python.

  • Design robust system architectures involving APIs, webhooks, databases, and authentication.

  • Build RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems using LLMs, embeddings, document retrieval, and vector databases.

  • Evaluate existing platforms and develop custom solutions when off-the-shelf tools are insufficient.

  • Apply software engineering and cybersecurity best practices to ensure secure, reliable, and maintainable systems.

Project Ownership & Collaboration

  • Take ownership of projects from requirements gathering and solution design through testing, deployment, and optimization.

  • Translate business requirements into practical technical solutions.

  • Collaborate with the founder and delivery team on technical decisions and project execution.

  • Maintain clear documentation and high standards of quality.

  • Proactively identify opportunities to improve systems, workflows, and development processes.

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

  • Several years (at least 3+) of professional software development experience, complemented by substantial hands-on automation engineering experience.

  • Advanced proficiency in n8n and Make.com, including complex, multi-step workflows and integrations.

  • Strong hands-on experience with HubSpot CRM, including its data structures, pipelines, properties, and automation capabilities.

  • Practical experience building RAG-based AI systems, including LLM integrations, embeddings, document retrieval, and vector databases.

  • Strong programming skills in JavaScript/TypeScript and/or Python.

  • Solid understanding of APIs, webhooks, databases, authentication, and system architecture.

  • Experience developing AI-powered workflows, LLM integrations, and AI agents.

  • Ability to independently design, troubleshoot, and deliver complex technical solutions.

  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate technical concepts clearly.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with Zapier, Close CRM, or other automation and CRM platforms.

  • Familiarity with Claude Code or similar AI-assisted development tools.

  • Experience building custom business applications or replacing/extending SaaS platforms.

  • Background in an AI automation consultancy, agency, or client-facing technical environment.

  • Previous technical leadership experience.

Ideal Candidate Profile

You're a software engineer at heart who understands both traditional development and modern automation platforms. You know when to use n8n or Make.com, when custom code is necessary, and how to design solutions that are secure, scalable, and maintainable.

You're analytical, structured, detail-oriented, and methodical in your approach. You think through technical challenges carefully, make logical and well-reasoned decisions, and value precision and quality over quick fixes.

You're also reliable, accountable, and calm under pressure. You take ownership of projects, communicate proactively, and can be trusted to deliver consistently high-quality work with minimal supervision.

Above all, you're curious about emerging AI technologies and motivated to build practical, innovative solutions that solve real business problems.

Why Join?

  • Work on complex AI automation, RAG, CRM integration, and custom software projects.

  • Collaborate closely with the founder of a growing AI consultancy serving the DACH market.

  • Take ownership of technical solutions with significant autonomy.

  • Help shape technical standards, processes, and future engineering capabilities.

  • Join a long-term, fully remote opportunity with room for professional growth.

  2. Client Interview

  3. Technical Assessment / Test Assignment

  4. Offer & Onboarding

The technical assessment will take place after the interview stage.

About Forterra

At Forterra, we are unleashing autonomy at scale to transform the battlefield. Our mission is to build the foundational platforms that enable an intelligent ecosystem to coordinate, adapt, and execute with speed and precision even in the uncertainty and disruption of modern conflict. In an era marked by rapid technological change and evolving threats, we design for flexibility, survivability, and operational dominance.

Forterra delivers weapons, sensors, and battlefield effects through integrated autonomous networks reaching operational areas faster, safer, and without placing human lives at risk. Our systems operate with distributed control, dynamic routing, and real-time responsiveness, enabling sustained advantage across complex mission environments.

About the role

Forterra is looking for a Lead Software Test Engineer to establish and run verification and validation for the safety critical embedded software used on our autonomous ground vehicles. This is initially an individual contributor role. You will set the software test approach, build the automation and test environments, execute the work, and maintain the evidence needed for customer and safety reviews. You will work closely with software, systems, and safety engineers to find problems early and make sure the software behaves correctly when things go wrong. As the capability grows, the role may develop into a technical lead for a small test team

Someone who can build a practical software test capability from the ground up and is comfortable working directly in the code, test environments, and evidence. This person should be able to work across software, systems, and safety engineering while staying focused on finding meaningful failures and making the product more dependable

What you'll do

  • Set the verification and validation approach for safety critical embedded software from kickoff through qualification, including the test plan, test procedures, results, and reports.
  • Turn system, software, and safety related requirements into practical tests with objective pass or fail criteria.
  • Maintain traceability between requirements, tests, results, and anomalies.
  • Build and maintain automated test frameworks for embedded software, including software in the loop and hardware in the loop environments.
  • Exercise failure behavior through fault injection, timing and jitter tests, communications failures, memory faults, power and clock faults, negative tests, boundary tests, and stress tests.
  • Use static analysis, dynamic analysis, and coverage results to find gaps and help the team close them.
  • Prepare and maintain test evidence, including plans, procedures, results, V&V matrices, compliance matrices, anomaly records, tool qualification records, and contributions to the safety case.
  • Work with software, systems, and safety engineers to review designs for testability, improve requirements, and support technical reviews and assessments.
  • Provide technical guidance through test plan reviews, design reviews, pairing, and mentoring.
  • Help establish the practices and infrastructure needed to grow a small software test capability.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Five or more years of experience testing embedded systems or safety critical software.
  • Strong working knowledge of C or C++ and Python for test automation.
  • Experience working with requirements management and requirements traceability using tools such as Jama or DOORS.
  • Familiarity with MISRA C or MISRA C++, static analysis, and structural coverage methods such as branch coverage and MC/DC.
  • Experience testing software on an RTOS such as QNX, including work with embedded targets, debuggers, and instrumentation.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to separate hardware, software, and firmware problems in a complex system.
  • A practical, organized approach to managing several priorities and producing clear technical documentation.
  • Ability to work remotely with up to 25% travel

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience applying safety critical development and assurance standards such as ISO 26262, IEC 61508,
  • DO-178C, MIL-STD-882E, JSSSEH, or JS-SSA-IG.
  • Experience with QNX, Linux, NXP S32G, or similar embedded platforms.
  • Experience with CAN, CAN-FD, Ethernet, UDS, J1939, or other vehicle networks and diagnostic protocols.
  • Understanding of robotics domains such as motion control, planning, perception, fault management, and vehicle interfaces.
  • Experience integrating electromechanical systems in automotive, aerospace, medical, industrial, defense, or similar environments.
  • Experience providing technical leadership through design reviews, mentoring, or improvements to shared test and development practices.

US Salary Range

$125,000.00.—$150,000.00 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate and is based on a wide variety of compensation factors. The salary offered to candidates will vary based on a variety of factors including (but not limited to) relevant work experience, education, specialized training, critical expertise, training, and more. Equity in Forterra is included in most of our full-time, high-demand roles and is therefore considered part of Forterra’s overall compensation package. In addition to base salary and equity, Forterra offers competitive benefits for full-time employees including:

  • Premium Healthcare Benefits: Three plan options, including an HSA-eligible plan, with Forterra covering 80% of the plan premium for you and your dependents.
  • Basic Life/AD&D, short and long-term disability insurance plans 100% covered by Forterra, plus the option to purchase additional life insurance for you and your dependents.

Element develops a sovereign, interoperable and secure communications platform for government, defence and public sector organisations.

You have the drive to help us grow as a company and to keep iterating on how we work, and you thrive in a strong engineering culture.

  • Experience working on open-source projects and/or contributing to the Matrix ecosystem.
  • Experience working with remote teams.

About the role.

You will play a pivotal role in making secure calling smooth, reliable and easy to adopt for the public-sector customers and community members who depend on us.

This is a hands-on, end-to-end product role. Calling is your anchor, but you will also drive our wider product objectives, including data-driven decision-making and the use of AI and LLM-powered tools to accelerate product delivery. You will collaborate closely with the rest of the product team and flex onto adjacent products or projects as our priorities evolve.

jobs.title: Senior Regulatory and Start Up Specialist (Mexico)
jobs.excerpt: We’re expanding our capabilities across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, and Peru, and we’re hiring a Senior Regulatory and Start Up Specialist (Senior RSS) in Mexico!
jobs.description:
We’re expanding our capabilities across Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, and Peru, and we’re hiring a Senior Regulatory and Start Up Specialist (Senior RSS) in Mexico!

As the Senior RSS on our team, you are a seasoned, experienced professional in regulatory and site start-up activities. Responsibilities will be dependent upon the location of the Senior RSS and include but are not limited to initial and subsequent clinical trial submission to Competent Authorities and IRB/Ethics Committees, Informed Consent Form review and adaptation, Essential Document collection and quality review, supporting sites on IRB/EC submissions and providing support to the Site Contract Management group in budget and contract negotiation.

The Senior RSS may act as Subject Matter Expert for questions by other in-country members (CRAs, CSSs or others) supporting site start-up activities, trainer for less-experienced staff on site start-up activities and may be identified as Owner of country specific tools and guidance documents to increase knowledge share of country specific site start-up activities and ensure compliance with local and international clinical trials regulations and guidelines.

Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to:

  • Responsible for delivery, in terms of timeliness and quality, of site activation readiness within the assigned country/sites and foreseeing and mitigating any risks
  • Preparation of Clinical Trial Application Forms as well as preparation of submission dossier (initial and amendments/notifications) for submission to Competent Authorities (CA), Ethics Committee (EC) and other applicable local bodies according to local requirements and within required timelines to obtain all necessary authorizations/approvals for the conduct of the Clinical Trial according to international and local/national applicable regulations, company SOPs and principles of ICH-GCP
  • Interaction with CA/EC for study purposes and handling responses to the CA/EC
  • Providing regular updates about CA and EC submissions to the Start Up Lead and/or Regulatory Lead assigned to the study and to Project Manager/Project Team as relevant
  • Maintenance of project plans, project trackers and regulatory intelligence tools as it pertains to assigned responsibilities and to keep Regulatory Leadership updated
  • Preparation/Support the development of study specific start-up plans, IMP release requirements and essential document review criteria
  • Partner with the assigned site CRA to ensure alignment in communication and secure site collaboration
  • Prepare, review and manage collection of essential documents required for site activation/IMP release
  • Customize country/site specific Patient Information Sheet and Informed Consent Forms.
  • Responsible for/facilitates the translation and co-ordination of translations for documents required for submission
  • Maintain communication with other key functions participating to country start up i.e., Feasibility, Clinical Operations, Project Management, Regulatory, and Site Contracts management group on project specific status and deliverables
  • Act as SME for collection and maintenance of site level critical path to Site Activation data points, including but not limited to Competent Authority, local IRB/Ethics Committee (EC) timelines, site contracts and budget negotiation requirements for and other required reviews to secure on time site activation for the assigned sites in the country
  • When required, participate/support the negotiation of study budgets and the execution of investigator contracts under directions of Site Contract Management department/designee department
  • Keep an updated knowledge of the local clinical trial laws, regulations and help distributing this knowledge within Precision for Medicine to ensure the conduct of Clinical Trials according to international and local/national applicable regulations
  • Maintain audit/inspection readiness at all times and file documents as per TMF plan and/ or study specific plans in the relevant TMF
  • May support the clinical team performing Pre-Study Site Visits
  • May participate/support feasibility group in site outreach to assess potential interest of investigators to a potential study
  • May support development of country specific Country Start-up summary and process flow identifying timelines, risks, and success factors
  • May support development of training sessions to expand Country Start-up knowledge and act as Subject Matter Expert for queries
  • May mentor staff on local study start-up regulations, submissions, and internal procedures
  • May interact with clients to provide activation readiness status updates, request documents or document review, and participate in proposal activities, including slide development and client presentation as required
  • Performs other duties as assigned by management

Qualifications

Minimum Required:

  • Bachelors’ degree in life sciences or related field (ideally in a scientific or healthcare discipline), or Registered Nurse (RN) or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience
  • 3.5 years or more as a Regulatory or SU specialist in either a CRO or pharmaceutical/ biotech industry or equivalent, relevant experience and/or demonstrated competencies
  • Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing at the English proficiently (Professional level)

Other Required:

  • Excellent communication and organizational skills are essential
  • Experience using computerized information systems, electronic spreadsheets, word processing and electronic mail required
  • Fluency in English and for non-English speaking countries the local language of country where position based
  • Ability to prioritize workload to meet deadlines

Preferred:

  • Relevant regulatory and site start-up (feasibility, contract negotiations, CA/EC/IRB submissions) experience for the particular country
  • Experience using milestone tracking tools/systems
  • Can assist junior SU specialists in problem resolution
  • Advanced degree in medical or life sciences (MD, PhD, PharmD)/RAC certification/Masters in Regulatory Science

Competencies:

  • Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements
  • Ability to follow task-specific procedures, be attentive to detail and place importance on accuracy of information
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Ability to effectively interact with project team(s) and effectively communicate in English and the local language of the country where located
  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment with a sense of urgency to match the pace
  • Must demonstrate excellent computer skills
  • Excellent communication, presentation, interpersonal skills, both written and spoken, with an ability to inform, influence, convince, and persuade
  • Flexible attitude with respect to work assignments and new learning
  • Occasional travel may be required

jobs.description:
Interested? Click here to apply now!

 

About the Role:

At TELUS Digital, we are advancing the future of Artificial Intelligence by helping AI systems understand, process, and generate human speech with greater accuracy and naturalness.

As an AI Speech & Audio Specialist in our AI Community, you will contribute to the development and improvement of next-generation speech AI technologies, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Text-to-Speech (TTS), Voice AI, and audio machine learning systems.

We rely on our global community of specialists to evaluate, create, refine, and improve high-quality speech and audio datasets. Your expertise in audio production, speech analysis, linguistics, or voice technology will help ensure AI models deliver natural, accurate, culturally relevant, and human-like voice experiences.

At TELUS Digital, you will play a key role in shaping how AI listens, understands, and communicates with people around the world.

 

Key Responsibilities:

·         Evaluate AI-generated speech (TTS) for naturalness, pronunciation accuracy, rhythm, tone, emotion, and overall voice quality.

·         Review and improve speech recognition outputs (ASR) by identifying transcription errors, pronunciation issues, accents, and linguistic nuances.

·         Perform professional audio editing tasks including segmentation, trimming, noise reduction, silence adjustment, and quality enhancement.

·         Analyze audio recordings using waveform and spectrogram-based tools to identify quality issues.

·         Support the creation and validation of high-quality speech datasets used for AI model training and evaluation.

·         Review voice recordings for clarity, consistency, articulation, and technical quality.

·         Perform audio quality checks including loudness levels, background noise detection, clipping, distortion, and export specifications.

·         Support voice AI projects including TTS, ASR, voice generation, voice similarity, voice mimicry, and conversational AI evaluation.

·         Apply expertise in phonetics, linguistics, audio engineering, or speech technology to improve AI-generated voice experiences.

 

Qualification path

Mandatory Qualifications:

Education / Professional Background:

Minimum of one of the following:

·         Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in:

·         Audio Engineering

·         Sound Engineering

·         Music Technology

·         Linguistics

·         Phonetics

·         Speech-Language Pathology

·         Computational Linguistics

·         Computer Science (Speech/AI focus)

·         Related audio or speech fields

 

OR

Professional experience in:

·         Sound design

·         Dialogue editing

·         Voice recording

·         Podcast/audio post-production

·         Speech data creation

·         Noise reduction

·         Speech segmentation

·         Spectrogram analysis

·         Audio quality assessment

·         Voice/audio processing workflows

Language Requirements:

·         Native-level proficiency (C1/C2+) in the required language is preferred for language-specific projects.

·         Ability to identify pronunciation, accent, and linguistic nuances.

·         English proficiency sufficient to understand technical instructions and project guidelines.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with:

·         Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)

·         Text-to-Speech (TTS)

·         Voice AI

·         Speech datasets

·         Audio annotation

·         Voice cloning or voice mimicry projects

·         ADR / dubbing

·         Localization audio

·         Broadcast or media production

·         AI model evaluation

 

Assessment:

·         Practical audio/speech evaluation (where applicable)

·         Identity verification process

 

The assessment may include:

 

·         Audio quality evaluation

·         Speech recognition review

·         Audio editing tasks

·         Voice quality analysis

·         Linguistic accuracy evaluation

 

Payment:

Currently, pay rates for specialists range from $6 - $40 USD per hour depending on expertise, project complexity, and market requirements. *Location and language is directly dependent.

Payment terms and rates are defined separately for each project engagement.

Why Join the TELUS Digital AI Community:

·         Community Connection: Work remotely as part of a 1M+ diverse global AI Community of contributors and experts.

·         Impactful Expertise: Use your native language and academic degree to shape real-world AI systems and products used by millions every day.

·         Hands-on Innovation: Gain experience in the latest AI research, evaluation, and fine-tuning methodologies.

·         Global Collaboration: Collaborate with a network of specialists across 20+ domains and 500+ languages and dialects.

·         Flexible Engagement: Manage your own schedule while making a meaningful impact on the future of technology.

 

TELUS Digital AI Community

Our global AI Community is a vibrant network of more than one million contributors from diverse backgrounds who help customers collect, enhance, train, translate, and localize content to build better AI models. Become part of our growing community and contribute to the development of innovative AI technologies used by some of the world's largest brands.

 

Independent Contractor Relationship:

This opportunity is offered on an independent contractor basis. Contributors have the flexibility to choose when and how much they work, subject to project availability and quality requirements. This opportunity is not and should not be construed as creating an employment relationship with TELUS Digital.

jobs.excerpt: Our customer's product is an AI-powered platform that helps businesses make better decisions and work more efficiently.
jobs.description:
Our customer's product is an AI-powered platform that helps businesses make better decisions and work more efficiently. It uses advanced analytics and machine learning to analyze large amounts of data and provide useful insights and predictions. The platform is widely used in various industries, including healthcare, to optimize processes, improve customer experiences, and support innovation. It integrates easily with existing systems, making it easier for teams to make quick, data-driven decisions to deliver cutting-edge solutions.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • Strong Python coding skills - 7+ years.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience with machine learning and production LLM systems.
  • Experience building backend APIs with FastAPI, async patterns, rate limiting, and SQLAlchemy - 3+ years.
  • Experience designing maintainable and extensible systems using dependency injection, interfaces, and abstract base classes.
  • Experience with vector databases such as Pinecone, Weaviate, or Chroma, as well as hybrid search.
  • Strong understanding of RAG architectures, including retrieval, reranking, context assembly, and response generation.
  • Hands-on experience with LangChain and LangGraph for building and orchestrating LLM workflows.
  • Advanced Python skills, including async/await, type hints, Pydantic, and SOLID principles.
  • MLOps experience with MLflow, model versioning, and A/B testing; experience with Langfuse is a plus.
  • Experience in NLP and computer vision, including document understanding, OCR, and GPT-4 Vision.
  • Experience building feature pipelines, real-time and batch inference systems, and model serving.
  • Hands-on experience with Hugging Face is required; experience with LlamaIndex is a plus.
  • Familiarity with database technologies such as SQL.
  • Good problem-solving skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

Nice to have skills:

  • Understanding of DevOps, CI / CD including: Docker containerization, Azure DevOps pipelines or GitHub Actions, Kubernetes (nice to have);
  • Data security including: Multi-tenant data isolation, Secure key management (Azure Key Vault), Audit trail implementation;
  • Experience in designing on cloud platform including: Azure (strongly preferred): Azure OpenAI, Blob Storage, Key Vault, Container Registry, AWS or GCP;
  • Experience in data engineering in Big Data systems including: Large-scale data processing, ETL/ELT pipelines.
  • Rate limiting and quota management for high-throughput API usage.
  • Cost management and optimization for LLM usage at scale.
  • Document processing expertise (PDF extraction, OCR tooling).
  • Production incident management and on-call experience.
  • Testing strategies for non-deterministic LLM outputs (e.g., golden datasets, fuzzy matching).
  • Domain knowledge in regulated industries (e.g., healthcare/pharma workflows, regulatory compliance) is a plus.

Responsibilities:

  • Build, refine, and use ML Engineering platforms and components; develop and implement scalable backend systems, APIs, and microservices using FastAPI.
  • Implement MLOps including model KPI measurement, tracking, model drift detection, and model feedback loops.
  • Deploy and operationalize ML and Deep Learning models, with a strong focus on LLMs and Generative AI.
  • Integrate Azure OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-4 Vision) and other LLM providers with proper retry logic and error handling.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of state-of-the-art technologies such as LLMs, GenAI, and transformer architectures.
  • Scale machine learning algorithms to work on massive data sets under strict SLAs.
  • Build and orchestrate model pipelines including feature engineering, inferencing, and continuous model training.
  • Write backend application code in Python and SQL using strong object-oriented principles and asynchronous programming (asyncio, async/await).
  • Implement dependency injection patterns and layered architecture (Service, Foundation, Orchestration, DAL).
  • Build LLM observability (e.g., Langfuse) to track prompts, tokens, costs, and latency.
  • Develop prompt management systems with versioning and fallback mechanisms.
  • Implement Celery (or similar) workflows for asynchronous task processing and complex pipelines.
  • Build multi-tenant architectures with client data isolation.
  • Implement cost optimization strategies for LLM usage (prompt caching, batch processing, token optimization).
  • Integrate third-party APIs and services (e.g., document/OCR services, cloud storage, enterprise systems).
  • Collaborate with client-facing teams to understand business context and contribute to technical requirement gathering.
  • Write production-ready code that is testable, maintainable, and accounts for edge cases and errors.
  • Ensure high quality of deliverables by following architecture/design guidelines, coding best practices, and periodic design/code reviews.
  • Write unit tests and higher-level tests to handle expected edge cases and errors gracefully.
  • Troubleshoot backend application code using structured logging and distributed tracing.
  • Use bug tracking, code review, version control, and other tools to organize and deliver work.
  • Participate in scrum calls and agile ceremonies, communicating progress, issues, and dependencies.
  • Document application changes and updates, including API documentation via OpenAPI/Swagger.
  • Research and evaluate emerging architecture patterns and technologies through rapid learning, proofs-of-concept, and prototypes.

Benefits

  • Awesome projects with an impact
  • Udemy courses of your choice
  • Team-buildings, events, marathons & charity activities to connect and recharge
  • Workshops, trainings, expert knowledge-sharing that keep you growing
  • Clear career path
  • Absence days for work-life balance
  • Flexible hours & work setup - work from anywhere and organize your day your way

jobs.title: National Consultant: A Gendered Analysis of Employment and Skills in the Large-S
jobs.excerpt: The International Institute for Sustainable Development is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges.
jobs.description:
The International Institute for Sustainable Development is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today's greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world. 

The Intergovernmental Forum on Mining, Minerals, Metals and Sustainable Development (IGF), working with project partners, including International Women in Mining, the International Labour Organization (ILO), Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, and the Environmental Governance Programme (EGP), jointly implemented by the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency and the United Nations Development Programme, completed the first phase of the Women and the Mine of the Future (WMF) project. Phase I established a gender-disaggregated employment baseline across 12 countries and culminated in the 2023 Women and the Mine of the Future: Global Report.

The IGF and ILO are now extending the global baseline through the addition of Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, and the United Kingdom. The purpose of this Terms of Reference is to commission a national baseline study for four new countries that is methodologically comparable with the original country studies and incorporates the most recent data available.

1. Background

Large-scale mining is being reshaped by rapid technological change, growing demand for minerals and metals needed for the energy and digital transitions, and increasing expectations for responsible and equitable mining. These shifts have significant implications for mining occupations, skills, working conditions, and labour market participation.

Reliable and comparable data are essential for understanding how women participate in the sector today and for designing policies that expand access to decent work and career progression. The first phase of the WMF project therefore focused on establishing a baseline of the gender-disaggregated profile of workers in large-scale mining. It covered Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Ghana, Mongolia, Peru, South Africa, Sweden, and Zambia and examined employment, occupations, education and skills, age, earnings and gender pay gaps where available, working conditions, and relevant policy and regulatory frameworks.

The 2023 Global Report demonstrated both the value of the baseline and the persistence of significant data gaps. Official labour market statistics are often fragmented, not consistently disaggregated by sex, or not available at a sufficiently detailed level for mining-specific analysis. Differences in national classifications, survey frequency, sample size, and data collection practices can also limit cross-country comparability. The extension of the baseline to four additional countries will broaden the geographical coverage of the evidence base and support future comparative analysis.

2. Rationale for Baseline Extension

The additional country studies should build directly on the methodology and lessons of the first phase. In particular, the studies should prioritize official national statistics and internationally comparable classifications; clearly distinguish between data that are directly comparable and data that are country-specific; and transparently document gaps, proxies, methodological limitations, and differences between data sources.

For consistency with the original Phase I baseline, the principal focus of this assignment is direct employment in large-scale mining. Artisanal and small-scale mining, oil and gas extraction, and indirect employment in mining supply chains are outside the core quantitative scope of this assignment. Where relevant, these issues may be referenced briefly to clarify national definitions or contextualize the findings.

3. Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective of the assignment is to prepare a country baseline study for the pilot countries (Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, and the United Kingdom) that can be integrated into the Women and the Mine of the Future global evidence base and compared, to the extent possible, with the 12 original country studies.

The specific objectives are to

  • compile and analyze the most reliable and recent gender-disaggregated data available on direct employment in the large-scale mining sector;
  • describe the profile of women and men in mining by occupation, age, education and skills, employment status and working arrangements, and earnings or pay gaps, where data permit;
  • review the policy, legal, and institutional context relevant to women’s employment, working conditions, equal opportunity, occupational health and safety, and career progression in mining;
  • identify key data gaps, inconsistencies, and methodological limitations and propose practical measures to strengthen future data collection and reporting;
  • identify relevant good practices and policy considerations that could improve women’s access to, retention in, and advancement within large-scale mining employment; and
  • generate standardized evidence that can be used in cross-country comparison and future updates of the global baseline.

4. Scope of Work

The standardized quantitative component of the baseline, including the extraction, harmonization, and analysis of labour market data using International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC) and International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO) classifications, will be undertaken separately by a statistician contracted under the IGF–ILO collaboration, drawing on the ILO database and methodology. The national consultant will complement this analysis through the collection and analysis of country-level quantitative data and evidence, contextual research, and assessment of the policy, regulatory, and institutional environment affecting women’s employment in large-scale mining.

The consultant is expected to

  • prepare an Inception Report outlining the proposed methodology, work plan, national data sources, relevant stakeholders, and approach to data collection and analysis. The report should identify anticipated challenges related to data availability, access, definitions, coverage, and comparability, with reference to the analytical framework in Appendix B.
  • collect complementary quantitative data and support the quantitative baseline analysis by identifying and accessing relevant national and sectoral data sources in line with the analytical framework in Appendix B. These may include labour force and establishment surveys, national mining employment statistics, administrative data sets, and data from ministries and government agencies, industry associations, mining companies, workers’ organizations, education and training institutions, and other relevant sources. The consultant will collect available sex-disaggregated data relevant to the analytical framework, particularly where such information is not available or sufficiently disaggregated in the ILO data set. The consultant may also liaise with relevant institutions to clarify data definitions, coverage, and limitations. The consultant will not be expected to produce or replicate the standardized ISIC- and ISCO-based data analysis undertaken separately under the IGF–ILO collaboration.
  • review relevant national laws, regulations, policies, strategies, and institutional arrangements concerning mining, labour and employment, gender equality and non-discrimination, occupational health and safety, maternity and parental protections, education and skills development, and other issues relevant to women’s participation and progression in the sector. The consultant will also review available evidence on workplace practices, working conditions, and barriers and enabling factors affecting women’s employment.
  • undertake a qualitative and policy analysis of women’s participation and employment conditions in large-scale mining, including barriers to recruitment, retention, and advancement; occupational segregation; workplace conditions and enabling factors; education, training, and skills pathways; and the extent to which relevant policy, regulatory, and institutional frameworks support women’s participation and progression in the sector.
  • identify and document relevant good practices by governments, mining companies, industry associations, workers’ organizations, and other relevant actors aimed at improving women’s participation, retention, working conditions, and career progression in the mining sector.
  • assess gaps and challenges in national systems for collecting, classifying, and reporting sex-disaggregated mining employment data and identify opportunities for improvement. In coordination with the IGF and ILO, the consultant will document country-specific definitions, coverage issues, discrepancies between national and international sources, and other limitations affecting interpretation or cross-country comparability, and identify practical opportunities to strengthen national data systems.
  • interpret and contextualize the quantitative findings produced by the IGF and ILO, together with the complementary quantitative evidence collected at country level, drawing on the wider country analysis to explain key patterns, disparities, and trends in women’s employment in large-scale mining.
  • propose practical policy recommendations to address identified barriers and strengthen women’s participation, retention, working conditions, and career progression in the large-scale mining sector.
  • prepare a Country Report that brings together the quantitative and qualitative evidence and presents the following:
    • the national mining, labour market, policy, regulatory, and institutional context,
    • key findings on women’s employment and participation in large-scale mining,
    • interpretation of the quantitative findings produced by the IGF and ILO and complementary country-level data,
    • barriers to women’s recruitment, retention, and advancement, including occupational segregation,
    • workplace conditions, enabling factors, and education and skills pathways,
    • good practices and relevant initiatives,
    • gaps and challenges in national sex-disaggregated mining employment data systems, and
    • practical policy recommendations to strengthen women’s participation, retention, working conditions, and career progression in the sector.
  • participate in regular coordination meetings with the IGF and ILO project team, and, where relevant, other national consultants to provide updates, clarify methodological issues, discuss emerging findings, and support consistency across the country studies.

The analytical framework guiding the study is provided in Appendix B. The national consultant is expected to use this framework to guide the collection and analysis of relevant national-level data and evidence. The standardized ISIC- and ISCO-based quantitative analysis will be produced separately through the IGF–ILO collaboration.

5. Profile of the National Consultant

The successful candidate will have an advanced university degree in economics, labour studies, gender studies, public policy, mining, social sciences, or another relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience. Additional qualifications include the following:

  • At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in mining, gender equality, labour and employment, public policy, or related research. Strong familiarity with the national mining sector is required.
  • Demonstrated experience in qualitative research, policy and institutional analysis, and high-quality analytical report writing, preferably on gender equality, employment, skills, or the extractives sector.
  • Ability to understand and interpret statistical findings and official labour market information, and to work effectively with a statistician or quantitative research team. Advanced microdata processing or ISIC/ISCO coding is not required for this assignment.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of gender equality issues affecting women’s participation, working conditions, retention, and advancement in the labour market; experience related to mining or other extractive industries is strongly preferred.
  • Ability to identify and critically assess official and non-official national sources, engage relevant institutions, and clearly explain country-specific definitions, data gaps, and contextual limitations.
  • Excellent written English. Fluency in the principal national language(s) required to access relevant legislation, policy documents, institutional information, and stakeholder perspectives.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to work independently while coordinating closely with an international project team.

6. Modalities of Work

The consultant will work closely with the IGF and ILO project team, which will provide methodological guidance, relevant materials from the first phase, and feedback on deliverables. The IGF will serve as the main administrative focal point unless otherwise specified in the contract.

The assignment is expected to be carried out primarily from the consultant’s home base. Meetings will normally be held remotely. Coordination meetings will be organized at key stages of the assignment and as needed to resolve methodological or data issues.

All deliverables will be submitted in English in editable formats. Quantitative data should be provided in the standardized spreadsheet format supplied by the project team, with clear source references and metadata sufficient to reproduce the analysis.

7. Budget

Applicants are invited to submit their expected daily rates. This information will be considered during the selection process.

8. Key Reference Materials

  • Women and the Mine of the Future project page:
  • Women and the Mine of the Future: Global Report (2023):
  • Women and the Mine of the Future Country Reports:
  • Methodological Note for WMF Baseline Data:

Please review the full Terms of Reference _ National Consultant , with particular attention to the following sections and appendices:

  • Delivery and Timeline Schedule
  • Appendix A: Countries Covered by the Women and the Mine of the Future Baseline
  • Appendix B: Analytical Framework for the Country Baseline
  • Appendix C: International Labour Organization’s Skills Level Classification and Comparability Guidance
  • Appendix D: Suggested Research Questions for Phase I, including Data Sources and Collection Methods

Application Process

Application deadline: November 20, 2026 4PM CST

All applications must be submitted in English.

To apply for this consultancy, interested applicants should submit the following:

  • Cover letter
  • Detailed CV highlighting relevant experience

NOTE:

  • Incomplete and late proposals will be automatically disqualified.
